body.text: Mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñī
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñī</s> (The Great Peacock Queen of Spells)

body.text: oṃ namo bhagavatyai āryamahāmāyūryai
body.translated_text: Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed <s>Āryamahāmāyūrī</s>!

body.text:
mṛtasaṃjīvanīṃ devīṃ duṣṭasatvanivāraṇīṃ
vidyā rājñīṃ mahātmānīṃ māyūrīṃ praṇamāmy ahaṃ
body.translated_text: I bow to <s>Māyūrī</s>, the goddess who revives the dead, who wards off evil beings, the great-souled queen of spells.

body.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyo 'rhadbhyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyaḥ sarvadharmamahāsaṃghebhyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones of the past, future, and present, and to all the great communities of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāya, namaḥ saptānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghānāṃ, namo loke 'rhatāṃ, namo maitreyapramukhānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ, namo 'nāgāmināṃ, namaḥ sakṛdāgāmināṃ, namaḥ śrotāpannānāṃ, namo loke samyaggatānāṃ, namaḥ samyakpratipannānāṃ. eṣāṃ namaskṛtvā imāṃ mahāmāyūrīṃ vidyārājñīṃ prayojayiṣyāmi. iyaṃ me vidyā samṛdhyatu, śṛṇvantu me bhūtagaṇāḥ. ye kecit pṛthivīcarāḥ khacarā jalacarā devā nāgā asurā marutā garuḍā gandharvāḥ kinnarā mahoragā yakṣā rākṣasāḥ pretāḥ piśācā bhūtāḥ kumbhāṇḍāḥ pūtanāḥ kaṭapūtanāḥ skandā unmādāś cchāyā apasmārā ostārakāḥ śṛṇvantu me ojāhārā bhūtagaṇā garbhāhārā rudhirāharā vasāhārā (Mmvr
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Homage to the seven perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> together with their communities of <s>śrāvakas</s>. Homage to the <s>Arhats</s> in the world. Homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> headed by <s>Maitreya</s>. Homage to the non-returners. Homage to the once-returners. Homage to the stream-enterers. Homage to those rightly gone in the world. Homage to those rightly practicing. Having paid homage to them, I shall employ this great <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Peacock Queen of Spells). May this spell succeed for me! Let the hosts of spirits hear me — whatever beings roam the earth, sky, or water: <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>marutas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>pūtanās</s>, <s>kaṭapūtanās</s>, <s>skandas</s>, madness-causing spirits, shadow-seizure spirits, epilepsy spirits, <s>ostārakas</s> — let them hear me! Essence-devourers, hosts of spirits, embryo-devourers, blood-devourers, fat-devourers,

body.text: māṃsāhārā medāhārā majjāhārā jātāhārā jīvitāhārā balyāhārā mālyāhārā gandhāhārā dhūpāhārāḥ puṣpāhārāḥ phalāhārāḥ sasyāhārā āhutyāhārāḥ pūjāhārārā viṣṭyāhārā mūtrāhārāḥ kheṭāhārāḥ śleṣmāhārāḥ śiṃghāṇakāhārā ucchiṣṭāhārā vāntāhārā aśucyāhārāḥ syandanikāhārāḥ, pāpacittāḥ duṣṭacittā raudracittāḥ paraprāṇaharāḥ. imāṃ mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñīṃ pravakṣyāmi, gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ baliṃ ca dāsyāmi, apakrāmantu me pāpacittāḥ duṣṭacittā raudracittāḥ paraprāṇaharāḥ sarvagrahā ojohārāḥ śṛṇvantu me, saumyacittā maitracittāḥ kalyāṇacittāḥ śṛṇvantu me buddhadharmasaṃghābhiprasannāḥ. tadyathā
body.translated_text: flesh-devourers, marrow-devourers, bone-marrow-devourers, birth-devourers, life-devourers, offering-devourers, garland-devourers, scent-devourers, incense-devourers, flower-devourers, fruit-devourers, crop-devourers, oblation-devourers, worship-devourers, excrement-devourers, urine-devourers, saliva-devourers, phlegm-devourers, mucus-devourers, leftover-devourers, vomit-devourers, filth-devourers, discharge-devourers — those of evil minds, malicious minds, fierce minds, those who take the lives of others! I shall recite this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peacock Queen of Spells) and shall offer incense, flowers, fragrance, lamps, and oblations. Let the evil-minded, malicious-minded, fierce-minded, and those who take the lives of others depart from me! Let the hosts of spirit-seizers who devour vitality hear me! Let those of benevolent minds, friendly minds, and wholesome minds, who are devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, hear me! Thus:

body.text: kāli karāli kumbhāṇḍi śaṃkhini kamalākṣi harīti harikeśi śrīmati hari haripiṅgale, laṃbe pralaṃbe kālapāśe kālaśodari yamadūti yamarākṣasi bhūtagrasani, pratīcchatha māṃ, gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ baliṃ ca dāsyāmi, rakṣatha mama sagaṇaparivārāṇāṃ sarvasatvānāṃś ca sarvabhayopadravebhyaḥ, jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ, sidhyantu me mantrapadāḥ svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Karālī</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Kamalākṣī</s>, <s>Hārītī</s>, <s>Harikeśī</s>, <s>Śrīmatī</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Haripiṅgalā</s>, <s>Lambā</s>, <s>Pralambā</s>, <s>Kālapāśā</s>, <s>Kālaśodarī</s>, <s>Yamadūtī</s>, <s>Yamarākṣasī</s>, <s>Bhūtagrasanī</s> — accept me! I shall offer incense, flowers, fragrance, and oblations. Protect me, together with my retinue, and all beings from all fears and calamities. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. May my <s>mantra</s>-words succeed! <s>Svāhā</s>!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmiṃ samaye bhagavāṃ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma, jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena mahatā bodhisatvasaṃghena sārdhaṃ, tena khalu punaḥ samayena śrāvastyāṃ jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍasyārāme svātir nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati sma. navo dahrataruṇo 'cirapravrajito 'ciropasaṃpanno 'cirāgata imaṃ dharmavinayaṃ, saṃghasyārthe jentākadārūṇi pāṭayamānaḥ, anyatamasmāt pūtidāruśuṣirān niṣkramya mahatā kṛṣṇasarpeṇa dakṣiṇe pādāṃguṣṭho daṣṭaḥ sa klāntakāyo bhūmau nipatitaḥ, phenaṃ vāhayamāno 'kṣiṇī ca parivartayamānaḥ svapiti.
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the garden of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> and a great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Now at that time, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the garden of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, there dwelt a <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Svāti</s>. He was new, young, recently gone forth, recently ordained, and had recently entered this <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>. While splitting firewood for the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s steam-bath, a great black cobra emerged from a certain rotten hollow log and bit him on the big toe of his right foot. His body became exhausted and he fell to the ground, foaming at the mouth and rolling his eyes, and lay unconscious.

body.text: adrākṣīd āyuṣmān ānandaḥ svātir nāma bhikṣum ābādhikaṃ duḥkhitaṃ gāḍhaglānaṃ bhūmau patitaṃ phenaṃ vāhayamānam akṣiṇī parivartayamānaṃ svapantaṃ, dṛṣṭvā ca punas tvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt. ekāntasthitaś cāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat. iha bhagavan chrāvastyāṃ jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍasyārāme svātir nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati, navo dahras taruṇo 'cirapravrajito 'ciropasaṃpanno 'cirāgata imaṃ dharmavinayaṃ. saṃghasyārthe jentākadārūṇi pāṭayamāno 'nyatamasmāt pūtidārusuṣirān niṣkramya mahatā kṛṣṇasarpeṇa dakṣiṇe pādāṃguṣṭho daṣṭaḥ. sa klāntakāyo bhūmau patitaḥ phenaṃ vāhayamāno 'kṣiṇī ca parivartayamānaḥ svapiti, tasyāhaṃ bhagavaṃ kathaṃ pratipadyāmi.
body.translated_text: The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> saw the <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Svāti</s> — afflicted, suffering, gravely ill, fallen on the ground, foaming at the mouth, rolling his eyes, and lying unconscious. Having seen this, he went quickly, quickly to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was. Having approached and bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here, <s>Bhagavān</s>, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the garden of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, there dwells a <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Svāti</s>. He is new, young, recently gone forth, recently ordained, and has recently entered this <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>. While splitting firewood for the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s steam-bath, a great black cobra emerged from a certain rotten hollow log and bit him on the big toe of his right foot. His body became exhausted and he fell to the ground, foaming at the mouth and rolling his eyes, and lies unconscious. How should I attend to him, <s>Bhagavān</s>?'

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam etad avocat. gaccha tvam ānanda tathāgatasya vacanenānayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣo rakṣāṃ kuru, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kuru. devagrahāto nāgagrahāto 'suragrahāto marutagrahāto garuḍagrahāto gandharvagrahātaḥ kinnaragrahāto mahoragagrahāto yakṣagrahāto rākṣasagrahātaḥ pretagrahātaḥ piśācagrahāto bhūtagrahātaḥ kumbhāṇḍagrahātaḥ pūtanagrahātaḥ kaṭapūtanagrahātaḥ skandagrahāto unmādagrahātaḥ chāyāgrahāto 'pasmāragrahāta ostārakagrahātaḥ kṛtyākarmaṇakākhordavetāḍakiraṇaciccakapreṣakadurbhuktaduścharditaduśchāyāduṣprekṣitadurlikhitadurlaṃghitāvadhūtātaḥ, (Mmvr
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, by the word of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peacock Queen of Spells), perform protection for the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāti</s> — perform guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, binding of the boundaries, and binding of the earth. [Protect him] from seizure by <s>devas</s>, from seizure by <s>nāgas</s>, from seizure by <s>asuras</s>, from seizure by <s>marutas</s>, from seizure by <s>garuḍas</s>, from seizure by <s>gandharvas</s>, from seizure by <s>kinnaras</s>, from seizure by <s>mahoragas</s>, from seizure by <s>yakṣas</s>, from seizure by <s>rākṣasas</s>, from seizure by <s>pretas</s>, from seizure by <s>piśācas</s>, from seizure by <s>bhūtas</s>, from seizure by <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, from seizure by <s>pūtanas</s>, from seizure by <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>, from seizure by <s>skandas</s>, from seizure by madness-spirits, from seizure by shadow-spirits, from seizure by epilepsy-spirits, from seizure by <s>ostārakas</s>, from sorcery, black magic, <s>ākhorḍa</s>-spells, <s>vetāḍa</s>-spells, <s>kiraṇa</s>-spells, <s>ciccaka</s>-spells, curses, ill-eaten food, ill-vomited, evil shadow, evil glance, evil scratching, evil stepping-over, and shaking-off afflictions,

body.text: jvarād ekāhikād dvaitīyakāt traitīyakāc cāturthakāt saptāhikād ardhamāsikān māsikād daivasikān mauhūrtikān nityajvarād viṣamajvarād bhūtajvarān mānuṣyajvarād amānuṣyajvarād vātikāt paittikāc chleṣmakāt sarvajvarāt, śirorttim apanaya ardhāvabhedakam arocakam akṣirogaṃ nāsārogaṃ mukharogaṃ kaṇṭharogaṃ hṛdrogaṃ galagrahaṃ karṇaśūlaṃ dantaśūlaṃ hṛdayaśūlaṃ pṛṣṭhaśūlaṃ pārśvaśūlaṃ udaraśūlaṃ maṇiśūlaṃ yoniśūlaṃ prajanaśūlaṃ gaṇḍaśūlaṃ vastiśūlaṃ ūruśūlaṃ jaṃghaśūlaṃ hastaśūlaṃ pādaśūlaṃ aṃgapratyaṃgaśūlaṃ cāpanaya.
body.translated_text: from fever — one-day fever, two-day fever, three-day fever, four-day fever, seven-day fever, half-month fever, monthly fever, daily fever, momentary fever, chronic fever, irregular fever, spirit-caused fever, human fever, non-human fever, wind-caused fever, bile-caused fever, phlegm-caused fever, and all fevers. Remove headache, half-head splitting, loss of appetite, eye disease, nose disease, mouth disease, throat disease, heart disease, throat-seizure, earache, toothache, heartache, backache, side-ache, stomachache, genital-ache, womb-ache, birth-ache, cheek-ache, bladder-ache, thigh-ache, shin-ache, hand-ache, foot-ache, and ache in every limb and joint.

body.text:
rātrau svasti divā svasti svasti madhyaṃdine sthite,
svasti sarvaṃ aho-rātraṃ sarvabuddhā diśantu me.
body.translated_text: May there be well-being at night, well-being by day, well-being when the midday stands, well-being through all day and night — may all the <s>Buddhas</s> grant this to me.

body.text: tadyathā
body.translated_text: Thus:

body.text:
maitrī me dhṛtarāṣṭreṣu maitrī airāvaṇeṣu ca,
virūpākṣeṣu me maitrī kṛṣṇagotamakṣeṣu ca.
maṇinā nāgarājena maitrī vāsukinā ca me,
daṇḍapādeṣu nāgeṣu pūrṇabhadreṣu me sadā.
nandopanandau yau nāgau varṇavantau yaśasvinau,
devāsuram api saṃgrāmam anubhavantau maharddhikau.
anavataptena varuṇena maitrī mandūrakena ca,
takṣakena anantena tathā vāsūmukhena ca.
aparājitena me maitrī maitrī cchitvāsutena ca,
mahāmanasvinānityaṃ tathaiva ca manasvinā.
kālako apalālaś ca bhāgavāñ chrāmaṇerakaḥ,
dadhimukho maṇiś caiva pauṇḍarīko diśāṃpatiḥ.
karkoṭakaḥ śaṃkhapālaḥ kambalāśvottarāv ubhau,
eteṣv api ca me maitrī nāgarājeṣu ca nityaśaḥ.

body.translated_text: May I have loving-kindness toward the <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭras</s> (nāgas), loving-kindness toward the <s>Airāvaṇas</s>; may I have loving-kindness toward the <s>Virūpākṣas</s>, and toward the <s>Kṛṣṇagotamakas</s>. May I have loving-kindness toward the <s>nāga</s>-king <s>Maṇi</s>, and toward <s>Vāsuki</s>; toward the <s>Daṇḍapāda</s> <s>nāgas</s>, and always toward the <s>Pūrṇabhadras</s>. <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, those two <s>nāgas</s>, resplendent and glorious, of great supernatural power, who have experienced even the war between gods and <s>asuras</s>. May I have loving-kindness toward <s>Anavatapta</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Mandūraka</s>, toward <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and likewise <s>Vāsūmukha</s>. May I have loving-kindness toward <s>Aparājita</s>, and toward <s>Chitvāsuta</s>, always toward <s>Mahāmanasvin</s>, and likewise toward <s>Manasvin</s>. <s>Kālaka</s>, <s>Apalāla</s>, <s>Bhāgavān</s>, <s>Śrāmaṇeraka</s>, <s>Dadhimukha</s>, <s>Maṇi</s>, and <s>Pauṇḍarīka</s>, lord of the directions. <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, <s>Śaṃkhapāla</s>, and both <s>Kambalāśvottara</s> — may I have loving-kindness always toward these <s>nāga</s>-kings as well. body.translated_text: <s>Sāketa</s>, the crocodile, and <s>Sūciloman</s> likewise; may I have loving-kindness toward the serpent-lord <s>Kāla</s> and toward <s>Ṛṣika</s>; likewise toward <s>Pūraṇakarṇa</s>, loving-kindness toward <s>Śakaṭamukha</s>, toward <s>Koluka</s>, <s>Sunanda</s>, and always toward <s>Vātsīputra</s>. May I have loving-kindness toward <s>Elapattra</s> and toward <s>Lamburaka</s>, and toward those <s>nāgas</s> who are non-human, and likewise those who are superhuman. <s>Mṛgila</s>, the great <s>nāga</s>, and <s>Mucilinda</s>, the renowned; those <s>nāgas</s> that dwell on the earth, and likewise those that abide in water; those that move through the sky, and those that dwell on <s>Meru</s> — single-headed, double-headed serpents — may I have loving-kindness toward them always. May I have loving-kindness toward the footless, loving-kindness toward the two-footed; may I have loving-kindness toward the four-footed, loving-kindness toward the many-footed. May the footless not harm me, may the two-footed not harm me; may the four-footed not harm me, may the many-footed not harm me. May I have loving-kindness toward all <s>nāgas</s>, those <s>nāgas</s> that abide in water; may I have loving-kindness toward all beings, whatever beings are stationed on the earth; may I have loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, whatever sentient beings here are immovable. May all sentient beings, all breathing creatures, all living beings whatsoever — may they all be happy, may they all be free from illness; may they all see auspicious things, may no one incur evil. Having aroused a mind of loving-kindness, I perform the neutralization of poison, the protection, the safeguarding, and likewise the guarding. Those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (holy ones) who have cast off evil qualities — homage to them, and may they protect me.

body.text: sarvabhayebhyaḥ sarvopadravebhyaḥ sarvopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ sarvajvarebhyaḥ sarvavyādhibhyaḥ sarvagrahebhyaḥ sarvaviṣebhyaḥ mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu, jīvantu varṣaśataṃ paśyantu śaradāśataṃ.
body.translated_text: From all fears, from all calamities, from all adversities and distresses, from all fevers, from all diseases, from all [malign] planetary seizures, from all poisons — may they grant protection to me and to all sentient beings. May they live a hundred years, may they see a hundred autumns.

body.text: bhūtapūrvam ānanda himavataḥ parvatarājasya dakṣiṇe pārśve suvarṇāvabhāso nāmo mayūrarājā prativasati sma. so 'py anayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā kalyaṃ svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā divā svastinā viharati. sāyaṃ svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā rātrau svastinā viharati.
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, <s>Ānanda</s>, on the southern slope of the <s>Himālaya</s>, king of mountains, there dwelt a peacock king named <s>Suvarṇāvabhāsa</s> (Golden Radiance). He, having performed the morning benediction with this <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peacock Spell Queen), would dwell in safety during the day. Having performed the evening benediction, he would dwell in safety during the night.

body.text: namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāya namo bhagavatyai mahāmāyūryai vidyārājñyai. tadyathā
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, homage to the Blessed <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s>. Thus:

body.translated_text: mountain-slope, greedy for sensual pleasures, attached, intoxicated by passion, deluded, infatuated, and agitated — through heedlessness he entered a certain mountain cave. There, for a long time, he was bound by enemies, adversaries, those who wished to harm, those who watched for an opportunity, those who sought an opportunity, in peacock-snares. He, having come into the midst of enemies, recovered his mindfulness, and brought this very <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s> to mind.

body.translated_text: Then he was freed from that calamity, and arrived safely and securely in his own domain. And he uttered these <s>mantra</s>-words:

body.translated_text: Unopposed everywhere! Protect! Protect me and all sentient beings! <s>Svāhā</s>. Homage to all the <s>Buddhas</s>. May there be well-being for <s>Svāti bhikṣu</s>, for me, and for all sentient beings. May they live a hundred years, may they see a hundred autumns. Thus:

body.text: huci guci muci svāhā.
body.translated_text: huci guci muci <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: syāt khalu punar ānanda anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena suvarṇāvabhāso nāma mayūrarājā babhūveti. na punar evaṃ draṣṭavyam. tat kasya hetoḥ. aham eva sa tena kālena tena samayena suvarṇāvabhāso nāma mayūrarājā babhūva. asyāś cānanda mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā etarhi hṛdayam anuvyākhyāsyāmi. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Ānanda</s>, you might think that the peacock king named <s>Suvarṇāvabhāsa</s> at that time, on that occasion, was someone else. It should not be viewed thus. For what reason? I myself was at that time, on that occasion, the peacock king named <s>Suvarṇāvabhāsa</s>. And now, <s>Ānanda</s>, I shall expound the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) of this <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s>. Thus:

body.text: ili mitti, tili mitti, tili mili mitti, tili mile, mili tili mitti, cili mili mili, cili mili mili, tili mili, sutumbā tumbā, suvaca cilikisiya, bhinna meḍi. namo buddhānāṃ cilikisi prāptamūle, itihārā lohitamūle, tumbā sutumbā kuṭṭi kunaṭṭi, tila kuñja naṭṭi, aḍakavātyāyāṃ, varṣatu devo nava māsān daśa māsān iti. ili mili kili mili keli mili, ketumūle, dudumbe sudumbe, sudumoḍe, dalime santuvaṭṭe busavaṭṭe, vusara vusara, dhanavastrake, narkalā narkalime, khalime ghoṣe rakhile iti, sajjale, tumbe sutumbe, aṭṭe naṭṭe pranaṭṭe aṇanaṭṭe, anamāle, varṣatu devo navodakena sarvataḥ samantena nārāyaṇi pārāyaṇi haritāli kuntāli, ili misti, kili misti, ili kili misti, ili me sidhyantu, drāmiḍā mantrapadāḥ svāhā.

body.text: idam ānanda mahāmāyūryā rājñyā hṛdayaṃ. iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī grāmagatena manasikartavyā, araṇyagatena manasikartavyā, pathigatena manasikartavyā, utpathagatena, rājakulamadhyagatena, cauramadhyagatena, agnimadhyagatena, udakamadhyagatena, pratyarthikamadhyagatena, parṣanmadhyagatena, vivādamadhyagatena, ahidaṣṭena, viṣapītena, sarvabhayasannipātena ca (Mmvr
body.translated_text: This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the heart of the great <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s>. And this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is to be called to mind by one who has gone to a village, by one who has gone to the forest, by one who has gone on a road, by one who has gone off the road, by one who is in the midst of a royal court, by one in the midst of thieves, by one in the midst of fire, by one in the midst of water, by one in the midst of adversaries, by one in the midst of an assembly, by one in the midst of a dispute, by one bitten by a snake, by one who has drunk poison, and in all convergences of danger,

body.text: manasikartavyā, jvaritena manasikartavyā. vātikapaittikaśleṣmikasānnipātikeṣu caturuttareṣu caturṣu vyādhiśateṣu, anyatarānyatareṇa vyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ samānāpatsu vāsam utpannāsu manasikartavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ. vadhyārho 'py ānanda daṇḍena mucyate daṇḍārhaḥ prahāreṇa, prahārārha ākrośena, ākrośārhaḥ, paribhāṣena, paribhāṣārho romaharṣaṇena, romaharṣaṇārha evam eva mucyate. sarvavyādhivinirvṛttiś cāsya bhaviṣyati. imāni cānanda vidyamantrapadāni manasikartavyāni. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: and it is to be called to mind by one who is feverish. In the four hundred and four diseases — those arising from wind, bile, phlegm, and their combination — when one is touched by any one of these diseases, when similar misfortunes arise, it is to be called to mind. For what reason? Even one deserving death, <s>Ānanda</s>, is freed from punishment; one deserving punishment is freed from blows; one deserving blows is freed from abuse; one deserving abuse is freed from reproach; one deserving reproach is freed from hair-raising terror — in this way one is freed. And all diseases will be cured for that person. And these <s>vidyā</s>-<s>mantra</s> words are to be called to mind, <s>Ānanda</s>. Thus:

body.text: cili mili kili mili ketumūle buddhavarṇe vusaraṇe vusaraṇe, vudāraṇi vudāraṇi, kevaṭṭe kevaṭṭakamūle, iti savale, tuṃbe tuṃbe, priyaṃ kare āvartta parivartta navodakena varṣatu devaḥ samantena. namo bhagavate iṭṭittāya indragomisikāya āśane pāśane pāpanikūle, kapilamitte ili mitte, namo bhagavate buddhāye, sidhyantu mantrapadāḥ mama sarvasatvānāñ ca svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>cili mili kili mili ketumūle buddhavarṇe vusaraṇe vusaraṇe, vudāraṇi vudāraṇi, kevaṭṭe kevaṭṭakamūle, iti savale, tuṃbe tuṃbe, priyaṃ kare āvartta parivartta</s> — may the god rain everywhere with fresh water. Homage to the Blessed <s>Iṭṭittā</s>, <s>Indragomisikā</s>, <s>Āśane</s>, <s>Pāśane</s>, <s>Pāpanikūle</s>, <s>Kapilamitte</s>, <s>Ili Mitte</s>. Homage to the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>! May the <s>mantra</s>-words succeed for me and for all beings! <s>Svāhā</s>!

body.translated_text: And with this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, perform protection for the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings — perform guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, binding of the boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. I do not see anyone, <s>Ānanda</s>, in this world with its <s>devas</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, among the population of ascetics and brahmins, of <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, who, when this protection has been performed with this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> — when the guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, binding of the boundaries, and binding of the earth have been performed — could approach to cause harm. body.text: citramūle citre citramāle, hale halamāle, phale phalamāle, hale hale, māle māle, khulu khulu vuru varuṇo, dhīre dharya, suru suru, hataṃ viṣaṃ, nihataṃ viṣaṃ, sarvaduṣṭapraduṣṭānāṃ draṃṣṭrāviṣaṃ mūlaviṣaṃ annaviṣaṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ tejasā, suru suru ke, cara cara ke, biri biri, hataṃ viṣaṃ, nāsti viṣaṃ, saptānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ, saśrāvakasaṃghānāṃ tejasā, ela melā, ili melā, tili melā, tiha duha tilimā timā dumā, vimadhu sukumbhā sumbhā tumbā samatumbā, āḍe nāḍe, tila kuñjanāḍe, varṣatu devaḥ, tilikisi samantena navamāsāṃ, maitrī me sarvasatveṣu vuśaḍe śavariṇi vudāriṇi vudāriṇi, kevaṭṭe kevaṭṭakamūle itiśabare, tuṃbe tuṃbe priyaṃ kare, āvaṭṭa parivaṭṭa, navodakena varṣatu devaḥ samantena, namo bhagavate indragomisikāya iṭṭitāya godohikāya bhṛṅgārikāya, ale tale kuntale, aṭṭe naṭṭe kunaṭṭe āśane pāśane, pāpanikūle pratikūle, namo bhagavatāṃ buddhānāṃ. sidhyantu mantrapadāḥ svāhā.
body.translated_text: citramūle citre citramāle, hale halamāle, phale phalamāle, hale hale, māle māle, khulu khulu vuru varuṇo, dhīre dharya, suru suru, the poison is destroyed, the poison is annihilated — the fang-poison, root-poison, and food-poison of all the evil and malicious ones — by the power of all the <s>Buddhas</s>, suru suru ke, cara cara ke, biri biri, the poison is destroyed, there is no poison, by the power of the seven Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddhas</s> together with their communities of <s>śrāvakas</s>, ela melā, ili melā, tili melā, tiha duha tilimā timā dumā, vimadhu sukumbhā sumbhā tumbā samatumbā, āḍe nāḍe, tila kuñjanāḍe, may the god rain, tilikisi, everywhere for nine months, may I have loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, vuśaḍe śavariṇi vudāriṇi vudāriṇi, kevaṭṭe kevaṭṭakamūle itiśabare, tuṃbe tuṃbe priyaṃ kare, āvaṭṭa parivaṭṭa, may the god rain with fresh water everywhere, homage to the Blessed <s>Indragomisika</s>, <s>Iṭṭita</s>, the house-lizard, the <s>Bhṛṅgārikā</s>, ale tale kuntale, aṭṭe naṭṭe kunaṭṭe āśane pāśane, at the evil bank, at the counter-bank, homage to the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. May the <s>mantra</s>-words succeed! <s>Svāhā</s>.

body.translated_text: may those deities, joyful in mind and elated, always grant peace and welfare.

body.text: tadyathā.
body.translated_text: Thus:

body.text: ili mili, kili mili, cili kili voli, udumbare, sudumoḍe, busara busara, hu hu, karañje karañjamūle, iti sanatā kuntari kuntāri, nārāyaṇi pārāyaṇi, paśyani paśya paśyani kapilavastuni, iḍivā iḍivā irivā sidhyantu, draviḍā mantrapadāḥ svāhā.
body.translated_text: ili mili, kili mili, cili kili voli, udumbare, sudumoḍe, busara busara, hu hu, karañje karañjamūle, iti sanatā kuntari kuntāri, <s>nārāyaṇi pārāyaṇi</s>, paśyani paśya paśyani, in <s>Kapilavastu</s>, iḍivā iḍivā irivā, may they succeed, the <s>Draviḍa</s> spell-words, <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: imāḥ punar ānanda mahauṣadhayo brahmaṇā sahāpatinā bhāṣitāḥ, śakreṇa devānām indreṇa caturbhiś ca mahārājair aṣṭāviṃśatibhiś ca mahāyakṣasenāpatibhiś ca. yo hy ānanda āsāṃ mahauṣadhīnāṃ nāmasu gṛhyamāneṣu kaścit praduṣṭacitta upasaṃkrāmet, saptadhāsya sphuṭo mūrdhā arjakasyeva mañjarī. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, these great medicinal herbs have been proclaimed by <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> (Lord of the World), by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, by the four great kings, and by the twenty-eight great <s>yakṣa</s> commanders. <s>Ānanda</s>, whoever should approach with a malicious mind while the names of these great medicinal herbs are being recited — his head will split into seven pieces, like the flower-cluster of an <s>arjaka</s> plant. Thus:

body.text: kīrttimūle eramūle eraṇḍamūle samantamūle, aḍanāḍe kuśanāḍe, itte mitte, pāru aḍakā maraḍakā, ilikiśi godohikā, udvandhamābhi bhinne medā. namo buddhānāṃ.
body.translated_text: kīrttimūle eramūle eraṇḍamūle samantamūle, aḍanāḍe kuśanāḍe, itte mitte, pāru aḍakā maraḍakā, ilikiśi godohikā, udvandhamābhi bhinne medā. Homage to the <s>Buddhas</s>.

svasti rātrau svasti divā svasti madhyaṃdine sthite,

body.translated_text: May there be well-being for the two-footed, may there be well-being for the four-footed; may there be well-being for those traveling on the road, and well-being for those who have returned. May there be well-being at night, well-being by day, well-being when the midday stands; may there be well-being everywhere for you — may evil not come upon any of them. May all days be auspicious, may all constellations be favorable. All <s>Buddhas</s> are of great supernatural power, all <s>Arhats</s> are free from outflows — (Mmvr

body.text: anena satyavākena svastir bhotu samantataḥ.
body.translated_text: by this truthful utterance, may there be well-being all around.

body.text: anayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā tathāgatabhāṣitayā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kuru, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kuru. jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ.
body.translated_text: By this <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s>, spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, perform protection for the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all sentient beings — perform guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, binding of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns.

body.text: ye cānanda yakṣā mahāyakṣāḥ samudrakūle prativasanti. ye ca sumerau parvatarāje, ye cānyeṣu parvatarājeṣu, aṭavīṣu mahāṭavīṣu nadīṣu mahānadīṣu kuṃjeṣu mahākuṃjeṣu viṇeṣu taḍāgeṣu palvaleṣu giriguhāśmaśāneṣu catvareṣu mahācatvareṣu catuṣpatheṣu śṛṅgāṭakeṣu nagareṣu mahānagareṣu ghoṣeṣu grāmeṣu udyāneṣu vaneṣu kānaneṣu patheṣu utpatheṣu ca, ye cānanda yakṣā mahāyakṣā aḍakavatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ prativasanti, te 'py anayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kurvantu, jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever <s>yakṣas</s> and great <s>yakṣas</s> dwell on the shore of the ocean, on <s>Sumeru</s> king of mountains, on other kings of mountains, in forests and great forests, at rivers and great rivers, in thickets and great thickets, in marshes, ponds, and pools, in mountain caves and cremation grounds, at crossroads and great crossroads, at four-way intersections and junctions, in cities and great cities, in hamlets and villages, in gardens and forests, in groves, on paths and by-paths — and whatever <s>yakṣas</s> and great <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, dwell in <s>Aḍakavatī</s>, the royal capital — may they too, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s>, grant protection to the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāti</s>, to me, and to all sentient beings — guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, binding of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. Thus:

body.text: hari hāriṇi, cali cālini, tramaṇi trāmaṇi mohani staṃbhani jaṃbhani svayaṃbhuve svāhā.
body.translated_text: hari hāriṇi, cali cālini, tramaṇi trāmaṇi, mohani (O Deluder!), staṃbhani (O Paralyzer!), jaṃbhani (O Crusher!), <s>svayaṃbhuve svāhā</s> (Hail to the Self-Existent One!).

body.text: pūrvāyām ānanda diśāyāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro nāma gandharvamahārājā prativasati, gandharvādhipatir anekagandharvaśatasahasraparivāro gandharvāṇām ādhipatyaṃ kārayati. yaḥ pūrvāṃ diśaṃ rakṣati paripālayati, so 'pi saputraḥ sapautraḥ sabhrātā sāmātyaḥ sasenāpatiḥ sapreṣyaḥ sadūtaḥ sapravaraḥ sapārṣado 'nayā mahāmāyūryā (Mmvr
body.translated_text: In the eastern direction, <s>Ānanda</s>, there dwells the great king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the <s>Gandharva</s> king, the lord of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of <s>Gandharvas</s>, exercising sovereignty over the <s>Gandharvas</s>. He who protects and guards the eastern direction — may he too, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, generals, servants, messengers, chief councilors, and retinue, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s> (Mmvr

body.text: vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ karotu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca karotu. jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: <s>vidyārājñī</s>, grant protection to the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāti</s>, to me, and to all sentient beings — guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, binding of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. Thus:

body.text: suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru me svāhā.
body.translated_text: suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru suru me <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: dakṣiṇāyām ānanda diśāyāṃ virūḍhako nāma kumbhāṇḍamahārājā prativasati sma, kumbhāṇḍādhipatir anekakumbhāṇḍaśatasahasraparivāraḥ kumbhāṇḍānām ādhipatyaṃ kārayati. yo dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ rakṣati paripālayati, so 'pi saputraḥ sapautraḥ sabhrātā sāmātyaḥ sasenāpatiḥ sapreṣyaḥ sadūtaḥ sapravaraḥ sapārṣado 'nayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ karotu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca karotu. jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: In the southern direction, <s>Ānanda</s>, there dwelt the great king <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s> king, the lord of the <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, exercising sovereignty over the <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>. He who protects and guards the southern direction — may he too, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, generals, servants, messengers, chief councilors, and retinue, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s>, grant protection to the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāti</s>, to me, and to all sentient beings — guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, binding of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. Thus:

body.text: veluke veluke amitraghātanī varuṇavati somavati veṇumālini veluni putrike co cū ci cū svāhā.
body.translated_text: veluke veluke, <s>amitraghātanī</s> (Destroyer of Enemies!), <s>varuṇavatī</s>, <s>somatvatī</s>, <s>veṇumālinī</s>, velunī, putrike, co cū ci cū <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: paścimāyām ānanda diśāyāṃ virūpākṣo nāma nāgamahārājā prativasati, nāgādhipatir anekanāgaśatasahasraparivāro nāgānām ādhipatyaṃ kārayati. yaḥ paścimāṃ diśaṃ rakṣati paripālayati, so 'pi saputraḥ sapautraḥ sabhrātā sāmātyaḥ sasenāpatiḥ sapreṣyaḥ sadūtaḥ sapravaraḥ sapārṣado 'nayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ karotu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ (Mmvr
body.translated_text: In the western direction, <s>Ānanda</s>, there dwells the great king <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king, the lord of the <s>Nāgas</s>, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of <s>Nāgas</s>, exercising sovereignty over the <s>Nāgas</s>. He who protects and guards the western direction — may he too, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, generals, servants, messengers, chief councilors, and retinue, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī</s>, grant protection to the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāti</s>, to me, and to all sentient beings — guarding, rescue, sheltering, safekeeping, pacification, blessing, warding off of weapons, warding off of blades, neutralizing of poison, destroying of poison, (Mmvr

body.text: sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca karotu. jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: may he establish a boundary-protection and an earth-binding. May [the practitioner] live a hundred years, may [the practitioner] see a hundred autumns. The formula is as follows:

body.text: veduri veduri veduri veduri, maṭṭite maṭṭite, koṭi koṭi, vidyumati, hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu, cu cu cu cu cu cu cu cu, ru ru ru ru ru ru ru ru, ca ca ca ca ca ca ca ca, sa svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>veduri veduri veduri veduri, maṭṭite maṭṭite, koṭi koṭi, vidyumati, hu hu hu hu hu hu hu hu, cu cu cu cu cu cu cu cu, ru ru ru ru ru ru ru ru, ca ca ca ca ca ca ca ca, sa svāhā</s>.

body.text: uttarāyām ānanda diśāyāṃ vaiśramaṇo nāma yakṣamahārājā prativasati, yakṣādhipatir anekayakṣaśatasahasraparivāro yakṣāṇām ādhipatyaṃ kārayati. ya uttarāṃ diśaṃ rakṣati paripālayati, so 'pi saputraḥ sapautraḥ sabhrātā sāmātyaḥ sasenāpatiḥ sapreṣyaḥ sadūtaḥ sapravaraḥ sapārṣado 'nayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ karotu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca karotu. jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: In the northern direction, <s>Ānanda</s>, dwells the <s>yakṣa</s> great king named <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>yakṣas</s>, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of <s>yakṣas</s>, exercising sovereignty over the <s>yakṣas</s>. He who guards and protects the northern direction — may he too, together with his sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, generals, servants, messengers, chief attendants, and retinue, by means of this Great <s>Māyūrī</s> Queen of Spells, provide protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for myself, and for all beings; may he provide shelter, rescue, care, safeguarding, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, boundary-protection, and earth-binding. May [the practitioner] live a hundred years, may [the practitioner] see a hundred autumns. The formula is as follows:

body.text: sori sori, siri siri, mati mati, hiri hiri, mati pele mati pele, piṃgale curu curu, hataṃ viṣaṃ, bandhumati, nihataṃ viṣaṃ bandhumati svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>sori sori, siri siri, mati mati, hiri hiri, mati pele mati pele, piṃgale curu curu, hataṃ viṣaṃ, bandhumati, nihataṃ viṣaṃ bandhumati svāhā</s>.

body.text:
pūrveṇa dhṛtarāṣṭras tu dakṣiṇena virūḍhakaḥ,
paścimena virūpākṣaḥ kuberaś cottarādiśaṃ.
catvāra ete mahārājā lokapālā yaśasvinaḥ,
diśaś catasraḥ paripālayanti mahāsainyā mahābalāḥ.
paracakrapramathanāḥ durdharṣā cāparājitāḥ,
ṛddhimanto dyutimanto varṇavanto yaśasvinaḥ,
devāsuram api saṃgrāmam anubhavanti maharddhikāḥ.
body.translated_text:
In the east is <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, in the south <s>Virūḍhaka</s>,
in the west <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and <s>Kubera</s> in the northern direction.
These four great kings, the glorious world-protectors,
guard the four directions, with great armies and great strength.
They crush the forces of enemies, invincible and unconquered,
possessing supernatural power, splendor, beauty, and glory;
these mighty ones prevail even in the battle between <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s>.

body.translated_text: Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, the names of the great <s>yakṣa</s> commanders who dwell upon the earth.

body.text:
jeṣṭhaputraḥ kuberasya saṃjayo naravāhanaḥ.
mithilāyāṃ prativasati devasatyopayācakaḥ.
body.translated_text:
The eldest son of <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Saṃjaya</s>, whose vehicle is a man,
dwells in <s>Mithilā</s>, one who fulfills the vows of the gods.

krakucchandaḥ pāṭaliputre ṣṭhalāyāṃ cāparājitaḥ,
śailo bhadrapure yakṣa uttarāyāṃ ca mānavaḥ.
vajrapāṇi rājagṛhe gṛdhrakūṭe kṛtālaye,
trikṛtvo anuparyanti sāgarān tāṃ vasuṃdharāṃ,
mahābalo mahātejā daśayojanavikramaḥ.
(Mmvr
body.translated_text:
<s>Krakucchanda</s> dwells in <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s> in <s>Sthalā</s>,
<s>Śaila</s> the <s>yakṣa</s> in <s>Bhadrapura</s>, and <s>Mānava</s> in <s>Uttarā</s>.
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s> in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, in <s>Kṛtālaya</s>,
he circles the oceans and the earth three times,
of great strength and great splendor, his stride spanning ten <s>yojanas</s>.

garuḍo vipule yakṣaḥ citraguptaś citīmukhe,
rājagṛhe vakkulo yakṣo mahāsainyo mahābalaḥ.
kālopakālakau yakṣau vasathaḥ kapilavastuni,
yatra jāto muni buddhaḥ śākyaketur mahāmuniḥ.
kalmāṣapādo vairāyāṃ kirāteṣu maheśvaraḥ,
bṛhaspatiś ca śrāvastyāṃ sākete sāgaro vaset.

chatrākāre veṣṭitakas tripuryāṃ makaraṃdamaḥ.
ekakakṣe viśālākṣo aṇḍabhaś ca udumbare,
anābhogaś ca vaiśālyāṃ śāntivatyāṃ virocanaḥ.
ahicchatre caritakaḥ kampilye kapilas tathā,
bakkulo ujjahānyāyāṃ maṇḍavyāṃ pūrṇakas tathā.
naigameśaś ca pāṃcālyāṃ prasabho gajasāhvaye,
varuṇāyāṃ dṛḍhadhanuḥ yodheye ca puraṃjayaḥ.
kurukṣetre ca yakṣendrau tararkakurutararkau,
yakṣīkhyātā ca tatraiva mahollūkhalamekhalau.
vyatipātanaḥ siddhārtha āyatīvānivāsinaḥ,
siddhapātras tathā śrughne sthalāyāṃ sthala eva ca.
yakṣau siṃhabalau yau tu siṃhavyāghrabalābalau,
koṭivarṣemahāsenas tathā parapuraṃjaye.
puṣpadantaś ca caṃpāyāṃ magadhaś ca giribraje,
goyoge parvato yakṣaḥ susenaś caiva nāgare.
vīrabāhuś ca sākete kākaṭyāṃ ca sukhāvahaḥ,
kauśāmbyāṃ cāpy anāyaso bhadrikāyāṃ ca bhadrikaḥ.
yakṣaḥ pāṭaliputre ca nāmnā bhūtamukhas tathā,
aśokaś caiva kāṃcīṣu ambaṣṭheṣu kaṭaṃkaṭaḥ.
bharukacche va siddhārtho mandakaś cājitaṃjaye,
agrodake maṃjakeśaḥ saindhave maṇikānanaḥ.
vikaṭaṃkaṭāś ca ye yakṣā vasante kapilavastuni,
gāndhārake naikṛtiko dvārako nilayadhruve.

<s>Veṣṭitaka</s> in <s>Chatrākāra</s>, and <s>Makaraṃdama</s> in <s>Tripurī</s>.
<s>Viśālākṣa</s> in <s>Ekakakṣa</s>, and <s>Aṇḍabha</s> in <s>Udumbara</s>,
<s>Anābhoga</s> in <s>Vaiśālī</s>, and <s>Virocana</s> in <s>Śāntivatī</s>.
<s>Caritaka</s> in <s>Ahicchatra</s>, and likewise <s>Kapila</s> in <s>Kampilya</s>,
<s>Vakkula</s> in <s>Ujjahānī</s>, and likewise <s>Pūrṇaka</s> in <s>Maṇḍavyā</s>.
<s>Naigameśa</s> in <s>Pāñcālya</s>, <s>Prasabha</s> in <s>Gajasāhvaya</s>,
<s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s> in <s>Varuṇā</s>, and <s>Puraṃjaya</s> in <s>Yodheya</s>.

and there too the <s>yakṣī</s> known as <s>Mahollūkhalamekhalā</s>.
<s>Vyatipātana</s> and <s>Siddhārtha</s>, dwellers of <s>Āyatī</s>,
and likewise <s>Siddhapātra</s> in <s>Śrughna</s>, and <s>Sthala</s> himself in <s>Sthalā</s>.
The two <s>yakṣas</s> <s>Siṃhabala</s>, possessing the strength of lion and tiger,
<s>Mahāsena</s> in <s>Koṭivarṣa</s>, and likewise in <s>Parapuraṃjaya</s>.
<s>Puṣpadanta</s> in <s>Campā</s>, and <s>Magadha</s> in <s>Girivraja</s>,
the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Parvata</s> in <s>Goyoga</s>, and <s>Susena</s> in the city.
<s>Vīrabāhu</s> in <s>Sāketa</s>, and <s>Sukhāvaha</s> in <s>Kākaṭī</s>,
<s>Anāyasa</s> in <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, and <s>Bhadrika</s> in <s>Bhadrikā</s>.
The <s>yakṣa</s> named <s>Bhūtamukha</s> likewise in <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>,
<s>Aśoka</s> among the <s>Kāñcīs</s>, and <s>Kaṭaṃkaṭa</s> among the <s>Ambaṣṭhas</s>.
<s>Siddhārtha</s> in <s>Bharukaccha</s>, and <s>Mandaka</s> in <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>,
<s>Maṃjakeśa</s> in <s>Agrodaka</s>, and <s>Maṇikānana</s> in <s>Saindhava</s>.

<s>Naikṛtika</s> in <s>Gāndhāraka</s>, and <s>Dvāraka</s> in the abode of <s>Nilayadhruva</s>.

yakṣo madhyamakīyaś ca saubhadriye mahāyaśe,
vairāṭakaḥ sārapure jambhako marubhūmiṣu.
yakṣo vṛndakaṭe khyātaḥ tathā vikaṭa ity api,
vemāniko devasarme daradeṣu ca mandaraḥ.
prabhaṃkaraś ca kaśmīre campakas ca jaṭāpure,
pāñcika iti nāmnā tu vasate siṃdhu siṃdhuṣu.
paṃcaputraśatā yasya mahāsainyā mahābalāḥ,
jeṣṭhaputraḥ pāñcikasya vasate cīnabhūmiṣu.
skandhākṣa iti nāmena sa bhrātā kauśike vaset,
uṣṭrapādaḥ kaliṃgeṣu maṇḍalo maṇḍalāsane.
laṃkeśvaraś ca kāpiśyāṃ mārīcī rāmakāṃkṣiyāṃ,
dharmapālaś ca khāśeṣu bahlyāñ caiva mahābhujaḥ.
jinarṣabho rājaputraḥ śrīmān vaiśramaṇātmajaḥ,
yakṣakoṭīparivṛtas tukhāreṣu nivāsikaḥ.
sātāgirihaimavatau vasataḥ siṃdhusāgare,
triśūlapāṇi tripure kaliṃgeṣu pramardanaḥ.
pāñcālagaṇḍo dramiḍe siṃhaleṣu dhaneśvaraḥ,
śukāmukhaś cāṭavyāṃ pātāle kiṃkaro vaset.
prabhāsvaraḥ puṇḍarīke samilaś ca mahāpure,
prabhaṃjanaś ca daradeṣu piṅgalo 'mbulime vaset.
vaccaḍo uaccaḍādhāne mātaliś caiva kāmade,

body.translated_text: The <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Madhyamakīya</s> is in <s>Saubhadriya</s>; <s>Mahāyaśas</s>, <s>Vairāṭaka</s> in <s>Sārapura</s>; <s>Jambhaka</s> in the desert lands. The <s>yakṣa</s> known as <s>Vṛndakaṭa</s>, and likewise the one called <s>Vikaṭa</s>; <s>Vemānika</s> in <s>Devasarman</s>; <s>Mandara</s> among the <s>Daradas</s>. <s>Prabhaṃkara</s> in <s>Kaśmīra</s>; <s>Campaka</s> in <s>Jaṭāpura</s>; the one named <s>Pāñcika</s> dwells in the <s>Sindhu</s> regions. He has five hundred sons, with great armies and great strength. The eldest son of <s>Pāñcika</s> dwells in the lands of <s>Cīna</s> (China). Named <s>Skandhākṣa</s>, his brother dwells in <s>Kauśika</s>. <s>Uṣṭrapāda</s> among the <s>Kaliṅgas</s>; <s>Maṇḍala</s> in <s>Maṇḍalāsana</s>. <s>Laṅkeśvara</s> in <s>Kāpiśī</s>; <s>Mārīcī</s> in <s>Rāmakāṃkṣiyā</s>; <s>Dharmapāla</s> among the <s>Khāśas</s>; and <s>Mahābhuja</s> in <s>Bāhlyā</s> (Bactria). <s>Jinarṣabha</s>, a prince, the glorious son of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, surrounded by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s>, dwells among the <s>Tukhāras</s> (Tocharians). <s>Sātāgiri</s> and <s>Haimavata</s> dwell at the <s>Sindhu</s> ocean. <s>Triśūlapāṇi</s> in <s>Tripura</s>; <s>Pramardana</s> among the <s>Kaliṅgas</s>. <s>Pāñcālagaṇḍa</s> in <s>Dramiḍa</s> (the Tamil lands); <s>Dhaneśvara</s> among the <s>Siṃhalas</s> (Sri Lanka). <s>Śukāmukha</s> in the forest; <s>Kiṃkara</s> dwells in <s>Pātāla</s> (the netherworld). <s>Prabhāsvara</s> in <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>; <s>Samila</s> in the great city. <s>Prabhaṃjana</s> among the <s>Daradas</s>; <s>Piṅgala</s> dwells in <s>Ambulima</s>. <s>Vaccaḍa</s> in <s>Vaccaḍādhāna</s>; <s>Mātali</s> in <s>Kāmada</s>. putrīvaṭe suprabuddhaḥ kāpiśyāṃ narakuveraḥ.
pārāsaraḥ pārateṣu śakasthāneṣu śaṃkaraḥ,
vemacitraś ca bāhlīke ketakeṣu ca piṅgalaḥ.
puṇḍavardhane pūrṇamukhaḥ karāḍaś coḍiyānake,
kuṃbhodaraḥ kauśaleṣu maruṣu makaradhvajaḥ.
citrasenaś ca vokkāne ramatheṣu ca rāvaṇaḥ,
piṃgalaś caiva rāśine patnīye priyadarśanaḥ.
kumbhīrayakṣo rājagṛhe vipule 'smiṃ nivāsikaḥ,
bhūyaḥ śatasahasrāṇāṃ yakṣeṇa paryupāsyate.
ahicchatrāyāṃ gopāla alako alakāpure,
nandī va nandinagare grāmaghoṣe baliḥ sthitaḥ.
devāvatāre vaiśramaṇaḥ svasainyaparipālakaḥ,
yakṣakoṭiparivṛto 'ḍakavatyāṃ nivāsikaḥ.
ete maharddhikā yakṣāḥ mahāsainyā mahābalāḥ,
paracakrapramathanā durdharṣā aparājitāh.
ṛddhimanto dyutimanto varṇavanto yaśasvinaḥ,
devāsuram api saṃgrāmam anubhavanti maharddhikāḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Suprabuddha</s> in <s>Putrīvaṭa</s>; <s>Narakuvera</s> in <s>Kāpiśī</s>. <s>Pārāsara</s> among the <s>Pāratas</s> (Parthians); <s>Śaṃkara</s> in the <s>Śaka</s> territories. <s>Vemacitra</s> in <s>Bāhlīka</s> (Bactria); <s>Piṅgala</s> among the <s>Ketakas</s>. <s>Pūrṇamukha</s> in <s>Puṇḍavardhana</s>; <s>Karāḍa</s> in <s>Oḍiyānaka</s> (Oḍḍiyāna). <s>Kumbhodara</s> among the <s>Kośalas</s>; <s>Makaradhvaja</s> in the desert regions. <s>Citrasena</s> in <s>Vokkāna</s>; <s>Rāvaṇa</s> among the <s>Ramathas</s>. <s>Piṅgala</s> in <s>Rāśina</s>; <s>Priyadarśana</s> in <s>Patnī</s>. The <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kumbhīra</s> in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, dwelling on this <s>Vipula</s> [mountain], is attended by further hundreds of thousands of <s>yakṣas</s>. <s>Gopāla</s> in <s>Ahicchatra</s>; <s>Alaka</s> in <s>Alakāpura</s>. <s>Nandī</s> in <s>Nandinagara</s>; <s>Bali</s> stationed in <s>Grāmaghoṣa</s>. <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (<s>Vaiśramaṇa</s>) in <s>Devāvatāra</s>, the guardian of his own army, surrounded by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s>, dwelling in <s>Aḍakavatī</s>. These <s>yakṣas</s> are of great supernatural power, with great armies and great strength, destroyers of enemy forces, invincible, unconquerable. body.translated_text: These are the twelve great <s>piśācīs</s> (female flesh-eating spirits), O <s>Ānanda</s>, by whom the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was protected while in his mother's womb, protected while being born, and protected after birth. Now, who are these twelve? They are as follows:

body.text: lambā pralambā vilambā olambā hārītī harikeśī piṅgalā kālī karālī kambugrīvā kākī kalaśodarī ceti. etā dvādaśa mahāpiśācyaḥ ṛddhimatyo dyutimatyo varṇavatyo yaśasvinaḥ, devāsuram api saṃgrāmam anubhavanti maharddhikāḥ. tā 'py anayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kurvantu, jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ. imāni cātra mantrapadāni bhavanti. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: <s>Lambā</s>, <s>Pralambā</s>, <s>Vilambā</s>, <s>Olambā</s>, <s>Hārītī</s>, <s>Harikeśī</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Karālī</s>, <s>Kambugrīvā</s>, <s>Kākī</s>, and <s>Kalaśodarī</s>. body.text: ābhir mahāvidyābhir mahāmantrair mahāpratisarābhir mahārakṣābhiḥ svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca hatāḥ kṛtyāḥ, hatāḥ karmaṇāḥ, hatāḥ kākhordāḥ kiraṇā vetāḍāś ciccāḥ preṣakāḥ, hatāḥ skandā unmādāś chāyā apasmārā ostārakāḥ, hatā uttrāsā garā viṣā, hatāḥ śoṣāḥ, hatā durbhuktakā duścharditā duśchāyā, hatā duḥprekṣitā dullikhitā durlaṃghitāḥ, avadhūtā hatāḥ. sarva jvarā ekāhikā dvaitīyakās traitīyakāś cāturthakāḥ saptāhikā ardhamāsikā māsikā daivasikā muhūrtikā nityajvarā viṣamajvarā bhūtajvarāḥ vātikāḥ paittikāḥ śleṣmikāḥ sānnipātikā mānuṣyajvarā amānuṣyajvarā hatāḥ, sarvajvarā dadrūkaṇḍūkiṭimakuṣṭhagaṇḍapiṭakapāmāvaisarpalohaliṅgā hatāḥ, śirorttiardhāvabhedakam arocakam akṣirogaṃ nāsārogaṃ mukharogaṃ kaṇṭharogaṃ hṛdrogaṃ galagrahaṃ karṇaśūlaṃ dantaśūlaṃ hṛdayaśūlaṃ pārśvaśūlaṃ pṛṣṭhaśūlaṃ udaraśūlaṃ gaṇḍaśūlaṃ vastiśūlaṃ gudaśūlaṃ yoniśūlaṃ prajanaśūlaṃ ūruśūlaṃ jaṃghāśūlaṃ hastaśūlaṃ pādaśūlaṃ aṅgapratyaṅgaśūlaṃ hataṃ. hatāḥ sarvagrahāḥ sarvaviṣāḥ sarvavyādhayaḥ. svastir bhavatu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca.
body.translated_text: By these great <s>vidyās</s> (spells), great <s>mantras</s>, great <s>pratisarās</s> (protective amulets), and great protective charms, for the well-being of the monk <s>Svāti</s>, myself, and all beings — destroyed are the <s>kṛtyās</s> (sorceries), destroyed are the <s>karmaṇas</s> (malefic rites), destroyed are the <s>kākhordās</s>, <s>kiraṇās</s>, <s>vetāḍas</s>, <s>ciccās</s>, and <s>preṣakas</s> (sending-spirits), destroyed are the <s>skandas</s> (seizure-spirits), <s>unmādas</s> (madness-spirits), <s>chāyās</s> (shadow-afflictions), <s>apasmāras</s> (epilepsy-spirits), and <s>ostārakās</s>, destroyed are terrors, poisons, and venoms, destroyed are the <s>śoṣas</s> (wasting diseases), destroyed are afflictions from bad food, bad vomiting, and bad shadow, destroyed are afflictions from evil glances, evil scratching, and evil stepping-over — all are shaken off and destroyed. All fevers are destroyed: quotidian, tertian, quartan, septan, half-monthly, monthly, daily, momentary, chronic fevers, irregular fevers, spirit-caused fevers, fevers of wind, bile, phlegm, and their combination, human fevers and non-human fevers — destroyed. All fevers with ringworm, itching, <s>kiṭima</s>, leprosy, boils, pustules, scabies, erysipelas, and discoloration — destroyed. Headache, half-head splitting pain, loss of appetite, eye disease, nose disease, mouth disease, throat disease, heart disease, throat-seizure, ear-ache, tooth-ache, heart-pain, side-pain, back-pain, stomach-pain, cheek-pain, bladder-pain, rectal-pain, uterine-pain, genital-pain, thigh-pain, shin-pain, hand-pain, foot-pain, pain in every limb and sub-limb — destroyed. Destroyed are all seizure-spirits, all poisons, all diseases. May there be well-being for myself and all beings.

homage to the fully liberated one, homage to full liberation.

body.translated_text: These and other <s>nāga</s> kings, O <s>Ānanda</s>, who in this circle of the earth send rain from time to time, thunder from time to time, flash lightning from time to time, and ripen the crops from time to time — who have beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, who have taken up the training precepts, who have gone for refuge in the Three Jewels, who are long-lived and endure for an aeon, who are freed from the fear of <s>Garuḍa</s>, from the fear of <s>Agnivālaka</s> (fire-tailed ones), from the fear of royal punishment, from the fear of earthquakes — who are bearers of the earth, who dwell in great jeweled palaces, who are long-lived, who are called great lords, who possess great supernatural power, great majesty, great enjoyments, great retinues, who shatter the forces of enemies, who possess miraculous power, radiance, beauty, and glory. These mighty ones partake even in the battle between <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s>. These <s>nāga</s> kings, together with their sons, grandsons, brothers, ministers, generals, servants, messengers, chief attendants, and assembly members — may they too, by means of this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peacock Queen of Spells), grant protection to the monk <s>Svāti</s>, myself, and all beings; may they grant safeguarding, rescue, shelter, care, peace, benediction, protection from punishment, protection from weapons, the neutralizing of poison, the destruction of poison, the sealing of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May [the protected one] live a hundred years, may [the protected one] see [Manuscript folio

body.text: śaradāśataṃ. svasti mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā.
body.translated_text: a hundred autumns. May there be well-being for myself and all beings, <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: ucchiṣṭasyānutsiṣṭasya mattasya pramattasya gacchatas tiṣṭhataḥ, niṣaṇṇasya śayanasya jāgrataḥ, āgatasya anāgatasya svasti rājabhayāc caurabhayād, agnibhayād udakabhayād, bandhakabhayāt, pratyarthikabhayāt, pratyamitrabhayād uttrāsabhayād, paracakrabhayād, durbhikṣabhayād, akālamṛtyubhayād, dharaṇīkampabhayāc caṇḍamṛgabhayāt. svasti devabhayād, nāgabhayād, asurabhayād, garuḍabhayād, gandharvabhayād, kinnarabhayān, mahoragabhayād, yakṣabhayād, rākṣasabhayāt, pretabhayāt, piśācabhayād, bhūtabhayāt, kumbhāṇḍabhayāt, pūtanabhayāt, kaṭapūtanabhayāt, skandabhayād, unmādabhayād, chāyābhayād, apasmārabhayād, ostārakabhayāt. svasti kṛtyākarmaṇakākhordakiraṇavetāḍaciccapreṣakadurbhuktaduścharditaduśchāyāduḥprekṣitadurlikhitadurlaṃghitāvadhūtabhayāt. svasti dadrūkaṇḍūkiṭimakuṣṭhagaṇḍakapiṭakapāmāvaisarpalohaliṅgaśoṣauttrāsabhayāt. svasti mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā. svasti sarvarogebhyaḥ.
body.translated_text: May there be well-being for one who has eaten, for one who has not excreted, for one who is intoxicated, for one who is heedless, for one who is walking, for one who is standing, for one who is seated, for one who is lying down, for one who is awake, for one who has arrived, for one who has not arrived — well-being from fear of kings, fear of thieves, fear of fire, fear of water, fear of imprisonment, fear of adversaries, fear of enemies, fear of terror, fear of invading armies, fear of famine, fear of untimely death, fear of earthquakes, fear of fierce beasts. May there be well-being from fear of <s>devas</s> (gods), fear of <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), fear of <s>asuras</s> (titans), fear of <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), fear of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), fear of <s>kinnaras</s> (half-human beings), fear of <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), fear of <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), fear of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), fear of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), fear of <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), fear of <s>bhūtas</s> (ghosts), fear of <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-shaped demons), fear of <s>pūtanas</s> (foul spirits), fear of <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> (corpse-demons), fear of <s>Skanda</s> (seizure), fear of madness, fear of shadow-affliction, fear of epilepsy, fear of <s>ostāraka</s> (evil-eye). May there be well-being from fear of <s>kṛtyā</s> (sorcery), <s>karmaṇa</s> (witchcraft), <s>ākhorda</s> (curses), <s>kiraṇa</s> (spells), <s>vetāḍa</s> (vampiric magic), <s>cicca</s> (cutting spells), <s>preṣaka</s> (sending-spells), ill-eaten, ill-vomited, ill-shadowed, ill-glanced, ill-scratched, ill-stepped-over, and shaking-off afflictions. May there be well-being from fear of <s>dadrū</s> (ringworm), <s>kaṇḍū</s> (itching), <s>kiṭima</s> (skin disease), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (leprosy), <s>gaṇḍa</s> (boils), <s>piṭaka</s> (blisters), <s>pāmā</s> (scabies), <s>vaisarpa</s> (erysipelas), <s>lohaliṅga</s> (iron-mark disease), <s>śoṣa</s> (consumption), and terror. May there be well-being for me and for all beings, <s>svāhā</s>. May there be well-being from all diseases.

body.text:
rātrau svasti divā svasti madhyaṃdine sthite,
svasti sarvam ahorātraṃ sarvabuddhā diśantu vaḥ.
namo 'stu buddhāya namo 'stu bodhaye,
namo 'stu muktāya namo 'stu muktaye.
namo 'stu śāntāya namo 'stu śāntaye,
namo vimuktāya namo vimuktaye.
body.translated_text: Well-being at night, well-being by day, well-being when the midday stands, well-being throughout the entire day and night — may all the <s>Buddhas</s> grant you this. Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, homage to enlightenment, homage to the liberated one, homage to liberation, homage to the peaceful one, homage to peace, homage to the fully freed one, homage to full freedom.

body.text: ye brāhmaṇā vāhitapāpadharmāḥ teṣāṃ namas, te mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kurvantu. jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ. (Mmvr
body.translated_text: Those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (holy ones) who have cast off sinful ways — homage to them. May they provide protection, safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth for me and for all beings. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. [Manuscript folio 43]

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī vipaśyinā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Vipaśyin</s>. Thus:

body.text: araḍe karaḍe maraḍe madavardhane avaśabare ture ture care care śabare parṇaśabare, hucu hucu, kuci kuci, muci muci, huci huci huci huci huci huci huci, muci muci muci muci svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>araḍe karaḍe maraḍe madavardhane avaśabare ture ture care care śabare parṇaśabare, hucu hucu, kuci kuci, muci muci, huci huci huci huci huci huci huci, muci muci muci muci svāhā</s>.

body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Śikhin</s>. Thus:

body.text: iḍi miḍi khire vikhire, hili hili hili, mili mili, tumūle, ambare ambarāvati, dumbe dumbe hili hili hili, kurvi kurvi kurvi, muci muci muci, svāhā.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī viśvabhuvā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Viśvabhu</s>. Thus:

body.text: morike morike morike kevaṇṭu maṇḍitike, hare hare hare hare hare hare, ghare ghare, khare khare, phare phare phare, phali nidanti nidantire, śakaṭi makaṭi, naṇḍa naḍini, śiri śiri śiri śiri śiri śiri svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>morike morike morike kevaṇṭu maṇḍitike, hare hare hare hare hare hare, ghare ghare, khare khare, phare phare phare, phali nidanti nidantire, śakaṭi makaṭi, naṇḍa naḍini, śiri śiri śiri śiri śiri śiri svāhā</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī krakucchandena samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Krakucchanda</s>. Thus:

body.text: hiḍi miḍi kuḍi miḍi, tuḍi kuḍi aḍi muḍi tuḍi tuḍi āḍe dante dantile śakari makāri thagari cagari kañcane kañcanāvati, śabare, bare bare bare bare bare bare, dante siddhi svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>hiḍi miḍi kuḍi miḍi, tuḍi kuḍi aḍi muḍi tuḍi tuḍi āḍe dante dantile śakari makāri thagari cagari kañcane kañcanāvati, śabare, bare bare bare bare bare bare, dante siddhi svāhā</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī kanakamuninā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā (Mmvr
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken [Manuscript folio 44]

body.text: cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Kanakamuni</s>. Thus:

body.text: tantule tatale tatale calate, tale tale tale tale, vire vijaye vijjadhare, araje araje virajāmati, mati mālini maṇḍe śirimaṇḍe, jvala jvala jvala jvala jvala jvala, bhadravati siddhi svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>tantule tatale tatale calate, tale tale tale tale, vire vijaye vijjadhare, araje araje virajāmati, mati mālini maṇḍe śirimaṇḍe, jvala jvala jvala jvala jvala jvala, bhadravati siddhi svāhā</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī kāśyapena samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. Thus:

body.text: aṇḍare paṇḍare kaṇḍare maṇḍare khaṇḍare jaṃbu juṃbunadi jaṃbuvati, matte maṇḍitike, amare siddhi, hara hara hara hara, paśu paśu paśu paśu paśupati svāhā siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>aṇḍare paṇḍare kaṇḍare maṇḍare khaṇḍare jaṃbu juṃbunadi jaṃbuvati, matte maṇḍitike, amare siddhi, hara hara hara hara, paśu paśu paśu paśu paśupati svāhā siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi svāhā</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī mayāpy etarhi śākyamuninā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by me as well, now, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Thus:

body.text: hili mili kili mili ilile katale ketumūle aḍamali ḍaphe ḍaphe busareke, busaṭṭa narakande katili bocalike kambu dāriṇikāya śabaraṃge tatuṭṭa bharaśebho vardhani prakṛti daṃṣṭra mili tale, īti hāse amale makule baṭṭa baṭṭa varṣantu, devaḥ samantā yathā sukhaṃ daśāsu dikṣu. namo bhagavataḥ kumudodakaṃ bhavatu, namo bhagavate iṭiṭāya godohikāya bhṛṅgārikāya, aruci maruci naṭṭa naṭṭa vajre vajranaṭṭe udayanapriye, ale tāle kuntāle kule tāle, nārāyaṇi pārāyaṇi, paśyani sparśani siddhyantu drāmiḍā mantrapadāḥ svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>hili mili kili mili ilile katale ketumūle aḍamali ḍaphe ḍaphe busareke, busaṭṭa narakande katili bocalike kambu dāriṇikāya śabaraṃge tatuṭṭa bharaśebho vardhani prakṛti daṃṣṭra mili tale, īti hāse amale makule baṭṭa baṭṭa</s> — may the <s>devas</s> (gods) send rain from all directions, as much as is pleasant, in the ten quarters. Homage to the Blessed One — may there be water of lotus-ponds. Homage to the Blessed One <s>iṭiṭāya godohikāya bhṛṅgārikāya, aruci maruci naṭṭa naṭṭa vajre vajranaṭṭe udayanapriye, ale tāle kuntāle kule tāle, nārāyaṇi pārāyaṇi, paśyani sparśani</s> — may the <s>Drāmiḍa</s> (Dravidian) <s>mantrapadas</s> (spell-words) be accomplished, <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: saṃyathedaṃ mayā śākyamuninā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. ānandena bhikṣuṇā svāter bhikṣor daṣṭasya svastyayanaṃ kṛtaṃ, evaṃ sarvasatvānāṃ (Mmvr
body.translated_text: Thus has this been spoken and approved by me, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. By the monk <s>Ānanda</s>, a benediction was performed for the monk <s>Svāti</s> who had been bitten, and likewise for all beings [Manuscript folio 45]

body.text: ca rakṣā kṛtā bhavatu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kṛtaṃ bhavatu. jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ.
body.translated_text: may protection be accomplished — safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī maitreyena bodhisatvena mahāsatvena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) <s>Maitreya</s>. Thus:

body.text: śiri śiri śiri, bhadre, jyoti jyoti jyoti, bhadre, hare hare hare, hariṇi hāriṇi, danti śabari śive śūlapāṇini, bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi, bodhisatve, bodhiparipācaṇīye svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>śiri śiri śiri, bhadre, jyoti jyoti jyoti, bhadre, hare hare hare, hariṇi hāriṇi, danti śabari śive śūlapāṇini, bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi, bodhisatve, bodhiparipācaṇīye svāhā</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī brahmaṇā sahāpatinā bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>. Thus:

body.text: hili hili hili hili, mili mili mili mili, mālini caṅkali, kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri, kiraye brahmāye ratnakaraṇḍake, viḍāphu viḍāphuse, dhara dhara, hara hara, hule hule, phuru phuru phuru phuru phuru svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>hili hili hili hili, mili mili mili mili, mālini caṅkali, kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri, kiraye brahmāye ratnakaraṇḍake, viḍāphu viḍāphuse, dhara dhara, hara hara, hule hule, phuru phuru phuru phuru phuru svāhā</s>.

body.text: hataṃ viṣaṃ nihataṃ viṣaṃ, buddhatejohataṃ viṣaṃ, pratyekabuddhatejohataṃ viṣaṃ, arhattejohataṃ viṣaṃ, anāgāmitejohataṃ viṣaṃ, sakṛdāgāmitejohataṃ viṣaṃ, śrotāpannatejohataṃ viṣaṃ, satyavāditejohataṃ viṣaṃ, brahmadaṇḍatejohataṃ viṣaṃ, indravajratejohataṃ viṣaṃ, viṣṇucakratejohataṃ viṣaṃ, agnitejohataṃ viṣaṃ, varuṇapāśatejohataṃ viṣaṃ, asuramāyāhataṃ viṣaṃ, nāgavidyāhataṃ viṣaṃ, rudraśūlatejohataṃ viṣaṃ, skandaśaktitejohataṃ viṣaṃ, mahāmāyūrīvidyāhataṃ viṣaṃ. bhūmyā saṃkrāmatu viṣaṃ, svastyayanaṃ bhavatu svāter (Mmvr
body.translated_text: The poison is destroyed, the poison is struck down. The poison is destroyed by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>. The poison is destroyed by the power of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one). The poison is destroyed by the power of the <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one). The poison is destroyed by the power of the <s>Anāgāmin</s> (non-returner). The poison is destroyed by the power of the <s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner). The poison is destroyed by the power of the <s>Śrotāpanna</s> (stream-enterer). The poison is destroyed by the power of truth-speaking. The poison is destroyed by the power of <s>Brahmā's</s> staff. The poison is destroyed by the power of <s>Indra's</s> thunderbolt. The poison is destroyed by the power of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> discus. The poison is destroyed by the power of <s>Agni</s> (fire). The poison is destroyed by the power of <s>Varuṇa's</s> noose. The poison is destroyed by <s>Asura</s> (titan) magic. The poison is destroyed by <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) spells. The poison is destroyed by the power of <s>Rudra's</s> trident. The poison is destroyed by the power of <s>Skanda's</s> spear. The poison is destroyed by the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyā</s> (Great Peahen Spell). May the poison pass into the earth; may there be a benediction for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, [Manuscript folio 46]

body.text: bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvaviṣād vatsanābhaviṣād halāhalaviṣāt kālakūṭaviṣād daṃṣṭrāviṣān mūlaviṣād vidyudviṣān meghasaṅkaṭaviṣāc cuṇḍaviṣād hṛṣṭiviṣān meghaviṣāt sarpaviṣād lūṭakīṭakakanabhamaṇḍūkamakṣikābhramaratryambukatrailāṭakaviṣād garuḍaviṣān manuṣyaviṣād amanuṣyaviṣāt śakraviṣād oṣadhiviṣād vidyāviṣāt. svasti sarvaviṣebhyaḥ svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā.
body.translated_text: for me, and for all beings — from all poisons: from <s>vatsanābha</s> (aconite) poison, from <s>halāhala</s> (cosmic) poison, from <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly) poison, from fang-poison, from root-poison, from lightning-poison, from storm-cloud poison, from <s>cuṇḍa</s> poison, from <s>hṛṣṭi</s> poison, from cloud-poison, from serpent-poison, from the poison of spiders, insects, beetles, frogs, flies, bees, water-creatures, and <s>trailāṭaka</s> creatures, from <s>garuḍa</s> (divine bird) poison, from human poison, from non-human poison, from <s>Śakra</s> (Indra's) poison, from herb-poison, from spell-poison. May there be well-being from all poisons for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings, <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārajñī śakreṇa devānām indreṇa bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s> (gods). Thus:

body.text: jalā jantule cāpeṭi jantule mathani ghaṭani grasani hari hari śiri dyoti śire tataru tataru, ṇabati siṃhā hā hā hā hā hā, siṃhe dhiti dhiti kuru kuru śabare vajre jyoti tuṭa tuṭasi, baṭa baṭasi, sili sili, kapile, kapilamūle hā hī hūm. sarvaduṣṭa praduṣṭānāṃ jaṃbhana karomi. hastapādāṅganigrahaṃ karomi. saha tridaśehi devehi ḍaṭaṅgini surapativarti vajra vajra vajra vajra vajra vajra vajrapataye svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>jalā jantule cāpeṭi jantule mathani ghaṭani grasani hari hari śiri dyoti śire tataru tataru, ṇabati siṃhā hā hā hā hā hā, siṃhe dhiti dhiti kuru kuru śabare vajre jyoti tuṭa tuṭasi, baṭa baṭasi, sili sili, kapile, kapilamūle hā hī hūm</s>. I perform the paralysis of all the wicked and corrupt. I perform the restraint of their hands, feet, and limbs. Together with the thirty <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>ḍaṭaṅginī surapativarti</s>, <s>vajra vajra vajra vajra vajra vajra vajrapataye svāhā</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārajñī caturbhir mahārājair bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca tadyathā.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the Four Great Kings. Thus:

body.text: jvala jvalana, tapa tapana, dhama dhamana, śara śaraṇa, nakuṭi nakuṭi, muṭi muṭi, sara sara, mara mara, hara hara, bhara bhara, titi tiri, ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa, dā dā dā dā dā, vā vā vā vā vā, hale hale hale hale hale, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svasti svasti svasti svasti svasti, mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>jvala jvalana, tapa tapana, dhama dhamana, śara śaraṇa, nakuṭi nakuṭi, muṭi muṭi, sara sara, mara mara, hara hara, bhara bhara, titi tiri, ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa, dā dā dā dā dā, vā vā vā vā vā, hale hale hale hale hale, siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi siddhi, svasti svasti svasti svasti svasti</s>, for me and for all beings, <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: svasti sarvapreṣakātaḥ, kālarātrītaḥ, kālapāśātaḥ, mṛtyudaṇḍātaḥ, brahmadaṇḍātaḥ, indradaṇḍātaḥ, ṛṣidaṇḍātaḥ, devadaṇḍātaḥ, nāgadaṇḍātaḥ, asuradaṇḍātaḥ, marutadaṇḍātaḥ, garuḍadaṇḍātaḥ, gandharvadaṇḍātaḥ, kinnaradaṇḍātaḥ, mahoragadaṇḍātaḥ, yakṣadaṇḍātaḥ, rākṣasadaṇḍātaḥ, pretadaṇḍātaḥ, piśācadaṇḍātaḥ, bhūtadaṇḍātaḥ, kumbhāṇḍadaṇḍātaḥ, pūtanadaṇḍātaḥ, kaṭapūtanadaṇḍātaḥ, skandadaṇḍātaḥ, unmādadaṇḍātaḥ, ostārakadaṇḍātaḥ, vetāḍadaṇḍātaḥ, rājadaṇḍātaḥ, cauradaṇḍātaḥ, agnidaṇḍātaḥ, udakadaṇḍātaḥ, sarvadaṇḍakuṇḍebhyaḥ, svastir bhavatu, svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu, jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ.
body.translated_text: May there be well-being from all sending-spells, from the dark night of death, from the noose of death, from the staff of death, from the staff of <s>Brahmā</s>, from the staff of <s>Indra</s>, from the staff of the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), from the staff of the <s>devas</s> (gods), from the staff of the <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), from the staff of the <s>asuras</s> (titans), from the staff of the <s>Maruts</s> (storm gods), from the staff of the <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), from the staff of the <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), from the staff of the <s>kinnaras</s> (half-human beings), from the staff of the <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), from the staff of the <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), from the staff of the <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), from the staff of the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), from the staff of the <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), from the staff of the <s>bhūtas</s> (ghosts), from the staff of the <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-shaped demons), from the staff of the <s>pūtanas</s> (foul spirits), from the staff of the <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> (corpse-demons), from the staff of <s>Skanda</s> (seizure), from the staff of madness, from the staff of <s>ostāraka</s> (evil-eye), from the staff of <s>vetāḍas</s> (vampires), from the staff of kings, from the staff of thieves, from the staff of fire, from the staff of water, from all staffs and cauldrons — may there be well-being. May they provide protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns.

body.text: udgṛhṇa tvam ānanda nadīrājñīnāṃ nāmāni. tadyathā.

body.translated_text: These and other great rivers that flow upon this earth-circle — in all those rivers dwell <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>Maruts</s> (storm gods), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>kinnaras</s> (half-human beings), <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), <s>bhūtas</s> (ghosts), <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-shaped demons), <s>pūtanas</s> (foul spirits), <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> (corpse-demons), <s>skandas</s> (seizure spirits), madness spirits, shadow spirits, epilepsy spirits, evil-eye spirits, those who feed on vitality, those who feed on embryos, those who feed on blood, those who feed on flesh, those who feed on fat, those who feed on marrow, those who feed on bone-marrow, those who feed on the newborn, those who feed on life-force, those who feed on vomit, those who feed on offerings, those who feed on garlands, those who feed on fragrance, those who feed on flowers, those who feed on incense, those who feed on crops, those who feed on oblations, those who feed on pus, those who feed on excrement, those who feed on urine, those who feed on phlegm, those who feed on mucus, those who feed on snot, those who feed on leavings, those who feed on impurities, those who feed on discharge — of various forms, misshapen forms, eye-like forms, endless forms, forms assumed at will, and wondrous forms, all residing there. May they too, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen), provide protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings — safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns.

body.translated_text: Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, the names of the <s>grahas</s> (planets), which, moving among the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), announce waning and waxing, happiness and suffering, prosperity, abundance and famine. Thus:

body.text:
sūryo grahaḥ, candro grahaḥ, bṛhaspatiḥ grahaḥ, śukraḥ,
grahaḥ, śaniścaro grahaḥ, aṅgāro grahaḥ, budho grahaḥ.
rāhur asurendro grahaḥ, dhūmraketur grahaḥ,
aṣṭāviṃśati nakṣatrāḥ saptasapta diśi sthitāḥ.
tārāgrahās tathā pañca rāhuketuś ca saptamaḥ,
mahātejo mahābalo maharddhikā mahātapāḥ.
sūryacandramasau caiva saptatriṃśad anūnakāḥ,
udayāstaṃgamasthānaṃ cakrasaṃkramaṇāyudhāḥ.
kṣayavṛddhikarā loke mahātejā maharddhikāḥ,
vidyāṃ samanumodantu suprasannena cetasā.
body.translated_text: <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) is a planet, <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) is a planet, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) is a planet, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) is a planet, <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) is a planet, <s>Aṅgāra</s> (Mars) is a planet, <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is a planet, <s>Rāhu</s> the lord of <s>asuras</s> is a planet, <s>Dhūmraketu</s> (the comet) is a planet. The twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) are stationed seven in each direction. The five star-planets and <s>Rāhu</s>-<s>Ketu</s> as the seventh — of great splendor, great power, great supernatural might, and great austerity. The Sun and Moon together make thirty-seven complete; their rising and setting stations are their orbiting weapons. Causing decline and increase in the world, of great splendor and great supernatural might — may they approve this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) with well-pleased minds.

body.text: te 'py anayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kurvantu, jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ.
body.translated_text: May they too, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen), provide protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings — safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns.

body.translated_text: These, <s>Ānanda</s>, are the ancient great <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) — authors of the <s>Vedas</s>, promulgators of <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulae), givers of curses, of fierce vows, of great splendor, and of accomplished prowess. May they too, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen), provide protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings — safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. Thus:

body.translated_text: Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, the names of the great lords of progeny — those <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), <s>Maruts</s> (storm gods), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>kinnaras</s> (half-human beings), <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), humans and non-humans, those born in animal wombs, in heavens, in hells, those of auspicious and inauspicious nature — who are established in the three worlds with innumerable blessings. Thus:
