body.translated_text: These, <s>Ānanda</s>, are the great-souled <s>prajāpatis</s> (lords of progeny) established for the protection of the community of beings, both moving and stationary. May they too, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen), provide protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings — safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns. And may they provide protection with these irresistible <s>mantrapadas</s> (spell-words) for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings. Thus:

body.translated_text: Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, the names of the great trees. Thus:

body.text: kāñcano nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, pippalo nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, aśvatthāno nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, kapitthāno nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, udumbalo nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, kapītuko nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, śālo nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, karṇikāro nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, tiniśo nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, bilvo nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, cūto nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ, nicūto nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: The great tree named <s>Kāñcana</s> (golden tree), the great tree named <s>Pippala</s> (sacred fig), the great tree named <s>Aśvatthāna</s> (bodhi tree), the great tree named <s>Kapitthāna</s> (wood-apple), the great tree named <s>Udumbala</s> (cluster fig), the great tree named <s>Kapītuka</s>, the great tree named <s>Śāla</s> (sal tree), the great tree named <s>Karṇikāra</s> (Indian laburnum), the great tree named <s>Tiniśa</s>, the great tree named <s>Bilva</s> (wood-apple), the great tree named <s>Cūta</s> (mango), the great tree named <s>Nicūta</s> (wild mango).

body.text: ity ete cānye ca mahāvṛkṣāḥ teṣv api ca devatāḥ prativasanti. tā 'py anayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā svāter bhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kurvantu, guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kurvantu, jīvatu varṣaśataṃ paśyatu śaradāśataṃ.
body.translated_text: These and other great trees — in them too dwell deities. May they too, by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen), provide protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings — safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth. May one live a hundred years, may one see a hundred autumns.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī saptabhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. tadyathā. vipaśyinā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca, śikhinā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca, viśvabhuvā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca, krakucchandena samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca, kanakamuninā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca, kāśyapena samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca, mayā caitarhi śākyamuninā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī maitreyena bodhisatvena mahāsatvena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā (Mmvr
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) that was spoken and approved by the seven Perfectly Awakened Ones. Thus: it was spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Vipaśyin</s>, spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Śikhin</s>, spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Viśvabhu</s>, spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Krakucchanda</s>, spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Kanakamuni</s>, spoken and approved by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and spoken and approved by me as well, now, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> was spoken and approved by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) <s>Maitreya</s> [Manuscript folio 57]

body.text: ca. brahmaṇā sahāpatinā bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. śakreṇa devānām indreṇa caturbhiś ca mahārājair dhṛtaraṣṭreṇa gandharvarājena virūḍhakena kumbhāṇḍarājena virūpākṣeṇa nāgarājena vaiśravaṇena yakṣarājena bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca. aṣṭāviṃśatibhiś ca gandharvasenāpatibhiḥ, aṣṭāviṃśatibhiś ca kumbhāṇḍasenāpatiḥ, aṣṭāviṃśatibhiś ca nāgasenāpatibhiḥ, aṣṭāviṃśatibhiś ca yakṣasenāpatibhiḥ, pāñcikena ca yakṣasenāpatinā, hārityā ca pañcaputraśataparivārayā bhāṣitā cābhyanumoditā ca.
body.translated_text: and by <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>; and by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s> (gods); and by the Four Great Kings — by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> the king of the <s>gandharvas</s>, by <s>Virūḍhaka</s> the king of the <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, by <s>Virūpākṣa</s> the king of the <s>nāgas</s>, and by <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> the king of the <s>yakṣas</s> — it was spoken and approved. And by the twenty-eight <s>gandharva</s> commanders, by the twenty-eight <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s> commanders, by the twenty-eight <s>nāga</s> commanders, by the twenty-eight <s>yakṣa</s> commanders, by <s>Pāñcika</s> the <s>yakṣa</s> commander, and by <s>Hāritī</s> with her retinue of five hundred sons — it was spoken and approved.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī anatikramaṇīyā devagraheṇa nāgagraheṇa asuragraheṇa marutagraheṇa garuḍagraheṇa gandharvagraheṇa kinnaragraheṇa
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) is not to be transgressed by seizure of <s>devas</s> (gods), seizure of <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), seizure of <s>asuras</s> (titans), seizure of <s>Maruts</s> (storm gods), seizure of <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), seizure of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), seizure of <s>kinnaras</s> (half-human beings),

body.text: mahoragagraheṇa
body.translated_text: seizure of <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents),

body.text: yakṣagraheṇa rākṣasagraheṇa pretagraheṇa piśācagraheṇa bhūtagraheṇa kumbhāṇḍagraheṇa pūtanagraheṇa kaṭapūtanagraheṇa skandagraheṇa unmādagraheṇa chāyāgraheṇa apasmāragraheṇa ostārakagraheṇa. anatikramaṇīyā sarvagrahaiḥ, anatikramaṇīyā sarvojāhāriṇībhiḥ, garbhāhāriṇyā vasāhāriṇyā māṃsāhāriṇyā medāhāriṇyā majjāhāriṇyā jīvitāhāriṇyā balyāhāriṇyā mālyāhāriṇyā rudhirāhāriṇyā jātāhāriṇyā gandhāhāriṇyā puṣpāhāriṇyā dhūpāhāriṇyā phalāhāriṇyā sasyāhāriṇyā āhutyāhāriṇyā pūyāhāriṇyā viṣṭāhāriṇyā mūtrāhāriṇyā kheṭāhāriṇyā śleṣmāhāriṇyā siṃhānakāhāriṇyā utsiṣṭāhāriṇyā vāntāhāriṇyā viriktāhāriṇyā aśucyāhāriṇyā syandikāhāriṇyā. anatikramaṇīyā kṛtyākarmaṇakākhordakiraṇavetāḍaciccapreṣakadurbhuktaduścharditaduśchāyāduḥprekṣitadurlikhitadurlaṃghitāvadhūtaiḥ. anatikramaṇīyā (Mmvr
body.translated_text: seizure of <s>yakṣas</s>, seizure of <s>rākṣasas</s>, seizure of <s>pretas</s>, seizure of <s>piśācas</s>, seizure of <s>bhūtas</s>, seizure of <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, seizure of <s>pūtanas</s>, seizure of <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>, seizure of <s>Skanda</s>, seizure of madness, seizure of shadow, seizure of epilepsy, seizure of evil-eye. It is not to be transgressed by any seizure; not to be transgressed by any who steal vitality, who steal embryos, who steal fat, who steal flesh, who steal marrow, who steal bone-marrow, who steal life-force, who steal offerings, who steal garlands, who steal blood, who steal the newborn, who steal fragrance, who steal flowers, who steal incense, who steal fruit, who steal crops, who steal oblations, who steal pus, who steal excrement, who steal urine, who steal phlegm, who steal mucus, who steal leavings, who steal vomit, who steal purgings, who steal impurities, who steal discharge. It is not to be transgressed by <s>kṛtyā</s> (sorcery), <s>karmaṇaka</s> (witchcraft), <s>ākhorda</s> (curses), <s>kiraṇa</s> (spells), <s>vetāḍa</s> (vampiric magic), <s>cicca</s> (cutting spells), <s>preṣaka</s> (sending-spells), ill-eaten, ill-vomited, ill-shadowed, ill-glanced, ill-scratched, ill-stepped-over, and shaking-off afflictions. It is not to be transgressed [Manuscript folio 58]

body.text: jvareṇa ekāhikena dvaitīyakena traitīyakena cāturthakena saptāhikenārdhamāsikena māsikena dvaimāsikena mauhūrtikena nityajvareṇa viṣamajvareṇa bhūtajvareṇa mānuṣajvareṇa amānuṣajvareṇa vātikena paittikena śleṣmikena sānnipātikena. anatikramaṇīyā sarvajvaraiḥ. anatikramaṇīyā śirorttyā ardhāvabhedakenārocakenākṣirogena nāsārogena mukharogena kaṇṭharogena karṇarogena hṛdayarogena galagrahena karṇaśūlena dantaśūlena hṛdayaśūlena pārśvaśūlena pṛṣṭhaśūlena udaraśūlena gaṇḍaśūlena vastiśūlena yoniśūlena prajanaśūlena jaṃghāśūlena ūruśūlena hastaśūlena pādaśūlena aṅgapratyaṅgaśūlena. anatikramaṇīya dadrūkaṇḍūkiṭimakuṣṭhabhagandaragaṇḍapiṭakapāmāvaisarpalohaliṅgaiḥ. anatikramaṇīyā sarvavyādhibhiḥ sarvaduṣṭaiḥ sarvaviṣaiḥ sarvabhayaiḥ. anatikramaṇīyā sarvakalikalahavigrahopadravopasargopāyāsaiḥ.
body.translated_text: by fever — whether one-day fever, two-day fever, three-day fever, four-day fever, seven-day fever, half-monthly fever, monthly fever, two-monthly fever, momentary fever, constant fever, irregular fever, spirit-caused fever, human fever, non-human fever, whether caused by wind, bile, phlegm, or the combination of all three. It is not to be transgressed by any fever. It is not to be transgressed by headache, by migraine, by loss of appetite, by eye disease, by nose disease, by mouth disease, by throat disease, by ear disease, by heart disease, by choking of the throat, by pain in the ears, by pain in the teeth, by pain in the heart, by pain in the sides, by pain in the back, by pain in the belly, by pain from boils, by pain in the bladder, by pain in the womb, by pain in the genitals, by pain in the calves, by pain in the thighs, by pain in the hands, by pain in the feet, by pain in every limb and joint. It is not to be transgressed by ringworm, itching, skin disease, leprosy, fistula, boils, blisters, scabies, erysipelas, and iron-mark disease. It is not to be transgressed by any affliction, by any malice, by any poison, by any fear. It is not to be transgressed by any quarrel, dispute, conflict, calamity, misfortune, or distress.

body.text: yaś cemām ānanda mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñīm atikramet tasya vajrapāṇiḥ saptadhā mūrdhānam arjakasyeva mañjarīṃ sphoṭayiṣyati. sarvabuddhabodhisatvapratyekabuddhaśrāvakānāṃ tejasā naṣṭa āloko naṣṭaś cetasaḥ. āryapudgalās tena visaṃvāditā bhaveyuḥ. catvāraś cainaṃ mahārājānaḥ kṣuraparyantaiḥ śastrair mahāntaṃ vyasanam āpādayeyuḥ. śakraś cāsya devānām indras tridaśagaṇaparivṛto vajreṇa mūrdhānam abhibhindyāt. brahmatejasā cāsya vibhūtir bhasmaṃ gacchet. anayā cānanda mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñyā yasya rakṣā kriyate sūtraṃ pratisarā cābadhyate, sa bādhyarho hy ānanda daṇḍena mokṣate daṇḍārhaḥ, prahāraiḥ prahārārhaḥ, ākrośena ākrośārhaḥ, paribhāṣaṇayā paribhāṣaṇārhaḥ, romaharṣeṇa romaharṣaṇārhaḥ, evam eva mokṣate. na (Mmvr
body.translated_text: And whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, should transgress this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> — <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> will split his head into seven pieces, like the blossom of an <s>arjaka</s> plant. By the power of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), and <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), he shall have neither splendor, nor light, nor peace of mind. He would be contradicted by the noble ones. The Four Great Kings would bring upon him great calamity with razor-edged weapons. And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, surrounded by the hosts of the Thirty-Three gods, would split his skull with the thunderbolt. And by the power of <s>Brahmā</s>, his possessions would turn to ashes. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, whoever is protected by this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s>, and upon whom the <s>sūtra</s> (scripture) and protective cord are bound — though deserving punishment, <s>Ānanda</s>, he is freed from punishment; though deserving blows, he is freed from blows; though deserving abuse, he is freed from abuse; though deserving reproach, he is freed from reproach; though deserving to have his hair stand on end with terror, he is freed even from that. [Manuscript folio 59]

body.text: cāsya rājabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati, na caurabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati, nāgnibhayaṃ bhaviṣyati, nodakena kālaṃ kariṣyati, na cāsya kāye viṣaṃ kramiṣyati, na śastraṃ kramiṣyati, sukhaṃ ciraṃ jīviṣyati, sthāpayitvā ānanda paurāṇāṃ svapnāṃ sukhaṃ ca prativibudhiṣyati, svastho nirupadravo niruttrāso nihatapratyarthiko nihatapratyamitro nirupahataḥ sarvaviṣabhayavinirmuktaḥ, sukhaṃ ciraṃ jīviṣyati, sthāpayitvā ānanda paurāṇaṃ karmavipākaṃ.
body.translated_text: Nor shall there be fear from kings for him, nor fear from thieves, nor fear from fire, nor shall he die by water, nor shall poison enter his body, nor shall weapons pierce him. He shall live happily for a long time — except, <s>Ānanda</s>, for the ripening of ancient <s>karma</s> (past deeds). And he shall awaken pleasantly from dreams, healthy, free from calamity, free from terror, with adversaries destroyed, with enemies destroyed, unharmed, liberated from all fear of poison — he shall live happily for a long time, except, <s>Ānanda</s>, for the ripening of ancient <s>karma</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ cānanda mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī ativarṣe anāvṛṣṭau coccārayitavyā. tataḥ sarve nāgā autsukyam āpadyante ativarṣaṃ grahīṣyati, anāvṛṣṭau ca dhārāpātaṃ kariṣyati, yāvat tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā abhiprāyo bhaviṣyati tāvad devo varṣiṣyati. asyāś cānanda mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyāḥ smaraṇād eva sarvabhayavairavāṇi praśamiṣyanti. kiṃ punar imāṃ sakalasamastām akhaṇḍaṃ dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati, svastyayanaṃ vā kuryāt.
body.translated_text: And this, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) should be recited during excessive rain and during drought. Then all the <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings) become eager — during excessive rain they will restrain it, and during drought they will produce a downpour, and the <s>deva</s> (god of rain) will rain as long as is the wish of that son or daughter of good family. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, by the mere remembrance of this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s>, all fears and enmities shall be pacified. How much more so when one holds, recites, and preserves it complete, whole and unbroken, or performs a benediction with it.

body.text: udgṛhṇa tvam ānanda imāṃ mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñīṃ. paryavāpnuhi dhāraya vācaya mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñīṃ sarvabhayavairapraśamanīṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye me bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīṇām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ ca. tadyathā.
body.translated_text: Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen). Master it, hold it, recite it — the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> that pacifies all fears and enmities — for the protection, shielding, and safeguarding of the four assemblies: my monks, nuns, male lay-followers, and female lay-followers. Thus:

body.text: yāvati dhāvati balaki kuru tulu me svāhā. rakṣa māṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>yāvati dhāvati balaki kuru tulu me svāhā</s>. Protect me and all beings, <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text:
rāgo dveṣaś ca mohaś ca ete loke trayo viṣāḥ,
nirviṣo bhagavān buddho buddhasatyahataṃ viṣaṃ.
rāgo dveṣaś ca mohaś ca ete loke trayo viṣāḥ,
nirviṣo bhagavaddharmo dharmasatyahataṃ viṣaṃ.
rāgo dveṣaś ca mohaś ca ete loke trayo viṣāḥ,
nirviṣo bhagavatsaṃgho saṃghasatyahataṃ viṣaṃ.
(Mmvr
body.translated_text: Passion, hatred, and delusion — these are the three poisons in the world; the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> is free from poison — by the truth of the <s>Buddha</s>, poison is destroyed. Passion, hatred, and delusion — these are the three poisons in the world; the Blessed <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) is free from poison — by the truth of the <s>Dharma</s>, poison is destroyed. Passion, hatred, and delusion — these are the three poisons in the world; the Blessed <s>Saṅgha</s> (community) is free from poison — by the truth of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, poison is destroyed. [Manuscript folio 60]

body.text:
yady alaṃ sarvabuddhānām arhatāṃ caiva yad yaśaḥ,
tathāgatasya tejena kṛtaṃ svastyayanaṃ mayā.
svātibhikṣor mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca hataṃ viṣam,
body.translated_text: If the glory of all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Arhats</s> (worthy ones) is sufficient, then by the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), a benediction has been performed by me. For the monk <s>Svāti</s>, for me, and for all beings — poison is destroyed.

body.text: mahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī svāter bhikṣor mama bhavatu.
body.translated_text: May the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) be for the monk <s>Svāti</s> and for me.

body.text: sādhu bhagavann ity āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya yena svātir bhikṣus tenopasaṃkramya svāter bhikṣor anayā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā rakṣām akārṣīt. guptiṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ cākārṣīt, vyutthitaś cāyuṣmān svātir bhikṣus tasmād ābādhād āyuṣmatā ānandena rakṣāsvastyayane kṛte.
body.translated_text: "Very well, Blessed One," said the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and circumambulated him three times, he approached the monk <s>Svāti</s> and performed a protection for the monk <s>Svāti</s> with this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen). He performed safeguarding, shelter, care, guardianship, peace, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, sealing of boundaries, and binding of the earth. And the venerable monk <s>Svāti</s> arose from that illness, the protection and benediction having been performed by the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānanda āyuṣmāṃś ca svātir bhikṣur yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntau, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavataḥ sarvaṃ yathā vṛttāntaṃ nivedya bhagavatānujñatau caikānte niṣaṇṇau.
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and the venerable monk <s>Svāti</s> approached the Blessed One, and having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, reported to the Blessed One everything as it had occurred, received the Blessed One's approval, and sat down to one side.

body.text: atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam uvāca. dṛṣṭas te mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñāḥ prabhāva iti. tathā vāditaṃ bhagavantam ānandaḥ praṇamyovāca. kim idaṃ bhagavan na viditaṃ bhaviṣyati. bhagavān punar uvāca. apy evānanda catvāro mahāsamudrāḥ śoṣaṃ gaccheyuḥ, pṛthivī vā ākāśam utpadyet, candrādityau vā pṛthivyāṃ nipatetāṃ, nadyo vā pratiśroto gaccheyuḥ, na ca tathāgatasya vacanam anyathā bhaved iti. atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma. tasmāt tarhi tvam ānanda imāṃ mahāmāyūrīṃ vidyārājñīṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīṇām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ cārocaya. sādhu bhagavann ity āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya imāṃ mahāmāyūrīṃ vidyārājñīṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadām ārocayati bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīṇām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ ceti.
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Have you seen the power of the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen)?" "It has been spoken truly," said <s>Ānanda</s>, bowing to the Blessed One. "How could this not be known, Blessed One?" The Blessed One further said: "Indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>, even if the four great oceans were to dry up, or the earth were to fly up into space, or the sun and moon were to fall upon the earth, or the rivers were to flow backwards — even then, the word of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One) would not become otherwise." Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should proclaim this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> for the protection, shielding, and safeguarding of the four assemblies — monks, nuns, male lay-followers, and female lay-followers." "Very well, Blessed One," said the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and having assented to the Blessed One, he proclaims this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> to the four assemblies — monks, nuns, male lay-followers, and female lay-followers.

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān, āttamanā āyuṣmān ānanda āyuṣmāṃś ca svātir bhikṣur, ye ca tasyāṃ parṣadi sannipatitāḥ sanniṣaṇṇāḥ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragayakṣārākṣasamanuṣyāmanuṣyās te ca sarve bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti.
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and the venerable monk <s>Svāti</s> rejoiced, and all those assembled in that gathering — <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>kinnaras</s> (half-human beings), <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), humans and non-humans — they all rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: samāptā ceyaṃ bhagavaty āryamahāmāyūrī vidyārājñī.
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the Noble Great <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen) of the Blessed One.

body.text: avinaṣṭā yakṣamukhāt pratilabdhā navaśatikā buddhabhāṣitā.
body.translated_text: Not lost, recovered from the mouth of a <s>yakṣa</s>, the nine-hundred-verse text spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: rakṣa māṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca svastiśreyo bhavatv iti.
body.translated_text: Protect me and all beings — may there be well-being and glory.

body.text: asyā mahāmāyūryā vidyārājñyā ayam upacāraḥ. apatitakapilagomayena śucau bhūmipradeśe gocarmamātraṃ sthaṇḍilam upalipya samutpannena kāryeṇa yena kenacid gomayena caturaśraṃ maṇḍalakaṃ kartavyaṃ. tatra ca madhye buddhapratimā paścimābhimukhā sthāpayitavyā, tasyā vāmapārśve mahāmāyūrīpustakalikhitā citrakarmakṛtā vā sthāpayitavyā, atha vā trayo mayūracandrikāḥ kapilagomaye niṣadya sthāpayitavyāḥ, tataḥ śvetārkapuṣpāṇi śvetakaravīrabilbapatrāṇi śirīṣapatrāṇi ca datvā baliṃ tilakṛsaratilodakaṃ caiva pāyasaṃ guḍapūrṇakayāvakamadhupūrṇakabhaktāṃ yathā lābhena datvā prāṅmukhena gugguludhūpaṃ ca datvā tato dakṣiṇapaścimottaramukhena caturdiśaṃ pūrvoktānāṃ caturdiśānāṃ yakṣāṇām agrahāṃ kurvatā vaktavyaṃ, āgacchadhvaṃ, puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ gandhaṃ baliṃ dīpaṃ ca pratīcchadhvaṃ, rakṣa māṃ sarvasatvānāṃś ca. Oṃ varade hūṃ (Mmvr
body.translated_text: This is the ritual procedure for this <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Peahen Spell-Queen): On a clean spot of ground smeared with unfallen tawny cow-dung, an area the size of a cow-hide should be prepared as a ritual platform. Whatever the occasion that has arisen, a square <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) should be made with cow-dung. In the center, an image of the <s>Buddha</s> should be placed facing west. On its left side, the written text of the <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s> or a painted image should be placed; alternatively, three peacock tail-feathers should be placed seated in tawny cow-dung. Then, offering white <s>arka</s> flowers, white oleander and <s>bilva</s> leaves, and <s>śirīṣa</s> leaves as <s>bali</s> (offerings), and giving sesame-rice-gruel, sesame-water, rice-pudding, cakes filled with jaggery, barley-cakes, cakes filled with honey, and cooked rice as available, and offering <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) incense facing east, then facing south, west, and north — making offerings to the <s>yakṣas</s> of the four directions mentioned earlier, one should say: "Come, accept the flowers, incense, perfume, offerings, and lamps. Protect me and all beings." <s>Oṃ varade hūṃ</s> [Manuscript folio 62]

body.text: hariṇi sphuṭ kāriṇi svāhā.
body.translated_text: <s>hariṇi sphuṭ kāriṇi svāhā</s>.

body.text: tatra guḍapūrṇapāyasaṃ ca pūrvāyāṃ diśi sthāpayitavyaṃ, gandharvāṇāṃ sa baliḥ, tilakṛsarasurāpūrṇakaṃ ca dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi sthāpayitavyaṃ, kumbhāṇḍānāṃ sa baliḥ. kṣīrapūrṇakaṃ pāyasaṃ ca paścimāyāṃ diśi sthāpayitavyaṃ, nāgasuparṇīnāṃ sa baliḥ. siṃdhupūrṇakaṃ dadhibhaktam uttarasyāṃ diśi sthāpayitavyaṃ, yakṣāṇāṃ sa baliḥ.
body.translated_text: There, rice-pudding filled with jaggery should be placed in the eastern direction — that is the offering for the <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians). Sesame-rice-gruel and a vessel filled with liquor should be placed in the southern direction — that is the offering for the <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-shaped demons). A vessel filled with milk and rice-pudding should be placed in the western direction — that is the offering for the <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings) and <s>suparṇīs</s> (divine birds). A vessel filled with <s>sindhu</s> (rock-salt water) and curd-rice should be placed in the northern direction — that is the offering for the <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits).

body.text: āryamahāmāyūrī nāma mahāvidyārājñī samāptā iti.
body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s>, the great <s>Vidyārājñī</s> (Spell-Queen), is complete.

body.text:
ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hy avadat,
teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ.
body.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One) has declared their cause, and that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great <s>Śramaṇa</s> (ascetic).
